a2-20-consolidation.prompt: Tell Lauren what you have learnt and what you are going to do.
cues: Say what you have learnt
Say what you are going to do
a2-20-consolidation.target: He aprendido mucho. Voy a empezar un nuevo capítulo.
a2-20-consolidation.english: I have learnt a lot. I am going to begin a new chapter.
a2-20-consolidation.canDo: I can use the main A2 structures to talk about experiences, memories and new beginnings.

a2-imperfectobasico-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Summers by the Lake
a2-imperfectobasico-01.scenario: At the language exchange in Hanoi, Meg asks what you used to do when you were little. You grew up near a lake.
a2-imperfectobasico-01.prompt: Tell Meg what you always did as a child.
cues: Say what you always did
Say what you normally did with friends
a2-imperfectobasico-01.target: De niño, siempre nadaba en el lago. Normalmente jugaba con mis amigos.
a2-imperfectobasico-01.english: As a child, I always swam in the lake. I normally played with my friends.
a2-imperfectobasico-01.canDo: I can form the imperfecto of regular -AR verbs.

a2-imperfectobasico-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Did You Live?
a2-imperfectobasico-02.scenario: At the café in Hanoi, Kaylee asks where you lived and what you ate when you were a student.
a2-imperfectobasico-02.prompt: Tell Kaylee where you lived and what you ate.
cues: Say where you lived
Say what you ate with friends
a2-imperfectobasico-02.target: Vivía en un apartamento pequeño. Comía con mis amigos cada día.
a2-imperfectobasico-02.english: I lived in a small flat. I ate with my friends every day.
a2-imperfectobasico-02.canDo: I can form the imperfecto of regular -ER and -IR verbs.

a2-imperfectobasico-03.title: Communicative Challenge: As a Child
a2-imperfectobasico-03.scenario: Carlos asks you what you were like as a child and where your family went at weekends.
a2-imperfectobasico-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you were like and where you went.
cues: Say what you were like
Say where you went on Saturdays
a2-imperfectobasico-03.target: De niño, era tímido. Los sábados íbamos al parque.
a2-imperfectobasico-03.english: As a child, I was shy. On Saturdays we went to the park.
a2-imperfectobasico-03.canDo: I can conjugate the three irregular imperfecto verbs: ser, ir, ver.

a2-imperfectobasico-04.title: Communicative Challenge: My Childhood Home
a2-imperfectobasico-04.scenario: At the language exchange, Meg asks what the house of your childhood was like.
a2-imperfectobasico-04.prompt: Describe your childhood house to Meg.
cues: Say what the house was like
Say what the weather was like
a2-imperfectobasico-04.target: Mi casa era pequeña pero acogedora. Hacía mucho frío y llovía.
a2-imperfectobasico-04.english: My house was small but cosy. It was very cold and it rained.
a2-imperfectobasico-04.canDo: I can use the imperfecto to describe past physical states, emotions, and appearances.

a2-imperfectobasico-05.title: Communicative Challenge: My Grandmother
a2-imperfectobasico-05.scenario: At the café in Hanoi, Kaylee asks about your grandmother when you were a child.
a2-imperfectobasico-05.prompt: Tell Kaylee about your grandmother and what you did while she cooked.
cues: Say what she was like
Say what she always brought
Say what you did while she cooked
a2-imperfectobasico-05.target: Mi abuela era muy cariñosa y siempre traía un pastel. Mientras ella cocinaba, yo jugaba.
a2-imperfectobasico-05.english: My grandmother was very affectionate and always brought a cake. While she cooked, I played.
a2-imperfectobasico-05.canDo: I can use all imperfecto forms fluently across -AR, -ER, -IR verbs and the three irregulars.

a2-imperfectobasico-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Sundays in the Past
a2-imperfectobasico-consolidation.scenario: Meg asks you to tell her about the Sundays of your childhood.
a2-imperfectobasico-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what your family did on Sundays.
cues: Say where you all went
Say what your grandmother did while you played
a2-imperfectobasico-consolidation.target: De niño, los domingos íbamos a casa de mi abuela. Mientras ella hacía la comida, nosotros jugábamos.
a2-imperfectobasico-consolidation.english: As a child, on Sundays we went to my grandmother's house. While she made the food, we played.
a2-imperfectobasico-consolidation.canDo: I can demonstrate command of all imperfecto forms: -AR (-aba), -ER/-IR (-ía), ser/ir/ver.

a2-imperfectocontraste-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Rain in the Park
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.scenario: At the language exchange in Hanoi, Kaylee asks what you were doing when it started to rain yesterday. You were walking in the park.
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.prompt: Tell Kaylee that you were walking in the park when suddenly it started to rain.
cues: Say what you were doing
Say what happened suddenly
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.target: Paseaba por el parque cuando, de repente, empezó a llover.
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.english: I was strolling through the park when, suddenly, it started to rain.
a2-imperfectocontraste-01.canDo: I can understand the core difference: imperfecto = background/habit, indefinido = specific completed event.

a2-imperfectocontraste-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Things at Once
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.scenario: At the language exchange, Kaylee asks what you did at home last night. You cooked and listened to music at the same time.
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.prompt: Tell Kaylee that you listened to music while you were cooking.
cues: Say what you were doing first
Say what else you were doing at the same time
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.english: While I was cooking, I was listening to music.
a2-imperfectocontraste-02.canDo: I can use 'mientras + imperfecto' to describe two simultaneous past actions.

a2-imperfectocontraste-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How I Felt
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.scenario: Carlos asks you how you felt yesterday when you went into your Spanish class for the exam. You were very nervous and afraid.
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you were very nervous and afraid when you went into the class.
cues: Say how you felt
Say what you did at that moment
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.target: Estaba muy nervioso y tenía miedo cuando entré en la clase.
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.english: I was very nervous and I was afraid when I went into the class.
a2-imperfectocontraste-03.canDo: I can use the imperfecto for past emotional and physical states.

a2-imperfectocontraste-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Wallet in the Park
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.scenario: Kaylee asks what happened on Sunday. It was a quiet Sunday, you were walking in the park and you saw a wallet.
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.prompt: Tell Kaylee about your quiet Sunday and the wallet you saw in the park.
cues: Say what kind of day it was
Say what you were doing and what you saw
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.target: Era un domingo tranquilo. Caminaba por el parque cuando vi una cartera.
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.english: It was a quiet Sunday. I was walking through the park when I saw a wallet.
a2-imperfectocontraste-04.canDo: I can use both tenses together in an extended past narrative.

a2-imperfectocontraste-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Stormy Night
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.scenario: Meg asks why you got home so late last night. It was midnight and it was raining a lot when you arrived.
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.prompt: Tell Meg that it was midnight and raining a lot when you got home.
cues: Say what time it was
Say what the weather was like
Say what you did
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.target: Era medianoche y llovía mucho cuando llegué a casa.
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.english: It was midnight and it was raining a lot when I got home.
a2-imperfectocontraste-05.canDo: I can use the imperfecto for weather, time, and scene-setting.

a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: News at Work
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.scenario: At the language exchange, Kaylee asks what happened at your office yesterday. You were working when you got an email, and your hands were shaking while you read it.
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.prompt: Tell Kaylee what you were doing when the email arrived and how you felt while you read it.
cues: Say what you were doing when the email arrived
Say how you felt while you read it
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.target: Trabajaba en la oficina cuando recibí un email. Mientras lo leía, me temblaban las manos.
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.english: I was working in the office when I received an email. While I was reading it, my hands were shaking.
a2-imperfectocontraste-consolidation.canDo: I can fluently distinguish imperfecto (background/habit/state) from indefinido (event/action).

a2-imperativoafirmativo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Hot Afternoon
a2-imperativoafirmativo-01.scenario: Your friend Ana is visiting your flat in Hanoi. She says she is hot and has not eaten today.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-01.prompt: Tell Ana to open the window and to eat something.
cues: Tell her to open something
Tell her to do something else
a2-imperativoafirmativo-01.target: Abre la ventana y come algo.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-01.english: Open the window and eat something.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-01.canDo: I can form affirmative informal commands (tú) for regular -ar, -er, and -ir verbs.

a2-imperativoafirmativo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Careful in the Street
a2-imperativoafirmativo-02.scenario: You are crossing a busy street in Hanoi with your friend Meg. She is walking ahead of you towards the traffic.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-02.prompt: Tell Meg to come here and to be careful in the street.
cues: Tell her to come to you
Tell her to be careful
a2-imperativoafirmativo-02.target: Ven aquí y ten cuidado en la calle.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-02.english: Come here and be careful in the street.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-02.canDo: I can use the 8 irregular affirmative tú commands: ven, di, sal, haz, ten, ve, pon, sé.

a2-imperativoafirmativo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Welcome to the Office
a2-imperativoafirmativo-03.scenario: You work at the front desk of an office in Hanoi. Mr. García arrives for his appointment.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-03.prompt: Politely tell Mr. García to come in, take a seat and wait a moment.
cues: Tell him to come in
Tell him to take a seat
Tell him to wait
a2-imperativoafirmativo-03.target: Pase, tome asiento y espere un momento, por favor.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-03.english: Come in, take a seat and wait a moment, please.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-03.canDo: I can form formal commands for usted and ustedes.

a2-imperativoafirmativo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Is the Square?
a2-imperativoafirmativo-04.scenario: A tourist stops you in the street in Hanoi and asks how to get to the square. It is two streets straight ahead, then right at the traffic light.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-04.prompt: Tell the tourist politely how to get to the square.
cues: Say to go straight ahead
Say where to turn
a2-imperativoafirmativo-04.target: Siga recto dos calles y gire a la derecha en el semáforo.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-04.english: Go straight ahead two streets and turn right at the traffic light.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-04.canDo: I can give clear step-by-step street directions.

a2-imperativoafirmativo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Grandmother's Tortilla
a2-imperativoafirmativo-05.scenario: Meg wants to make the tortilla with the recipe of Carlos's grandmother. She asks you for the first steps.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-05.prompt: Tell Meg to cut the potatoes, heat the oil and add a pinch of salt.
cues: Say what to cut
Say what to heat
Say what to add
a2-imperativoafirmativo-05.target: Corta las papas, calienta el aceite y añade una pizca de sal.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-05.english: Cut the potatoes, heat the oil and add a pinch of salt.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-05.canDo: I can follow a Spanish recipe using imperative steps.

a2-imperativoafirmativo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Ways to Say It
a2-imperativoafirmativo-consolidation.scenario: At the language exchange you are helping. Your friend Kaylee needs to come to the table, and Mr. García, a visitor, needs a seat.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Kaylee (tú) to come here and tell Mr. García (usted) to take a seat.
cues: Tell Kaylee to come
Tell Mr. García to sit, politely
a2-imperativoafirmativo-consolidation.target: Kaylee, ven aquí. Señor García, tome asiento, por favor.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-consolidation.english: Kaylee, come here. Mr. García, take a seat, please.
a2-imperativoafirmativo-consolidation.canDo: I can give instructions with tú and usted commands, including the eight irregular ones.

a2-imperativonegativo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Do Not Worry
a2-imperativonegativo-01.scenario: Your friend Meg is late for the train in Hội An and is rushing through the station.
a2-imperativonegativo-01.prompt: Tell Meg not to worry and not to run.
cues: Tell her not to worry
Tell her not to run
a2-imperativonegativo-01.target: No te preocupes y no corras.
a2-imperativonegativo-01.canDo: I can tell someone not to do something using negative tú commands.

a2-imperativonegativo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Not Alone at Night
a2-imperativonegativo-02.scenario: At the hostel your friend Carlos wants to walk to the park alone, and it is already dark.
a2-imperativonegativo-02.prompt: Tell Carlos not to go alone and not to come back late.
cues: Tell him not to go alone
Tell him not to come late
a2-imperativonegativo-02.target: No vayas solo y no vengas tarde.
a2-imperativonegativo-02.english: Don't go alone and don't come late.
a2-imperativonegativo-02.canDo: I can tell friends not to go, do, say, or leave using irregular negative commands.

a2-imperativonegativo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: No Smoking, Please
a2-imperativonegativo-03.scenario: You work at the reception of the hostel in Hội An. A guest is about to smoke in the building.
a2-imperativonegativo-03.prompt: Politely tell the guest that he must not smoke in the building.
cues: Address him politely
Say what he must not do
a2-imperativonegativo-03.target: Señor, no fume en el edificio, por favor.
a2-imperativonegativo-03.english: Sir, please do not smoke in the building.
a2-imperativonegativo-03.canDo: I can formulate polite prohibitions and requests for strangers and groups.

a2-imperativonegativo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Sit Here
a2-imperativonegativo-04.scenario: Your friend Meg arrives at the hostel tired after the trip.
a2-imperativonegativo-04.prompt: Tell Meg to sit down here and not to get up yet.
cues: Tell her to sit down
Tell her not to get up
a2-imperativonegativo-04.target: Siéntate aquí y no te levantes todavía.
a2-imperativonegativo-04.english: Sit down here and don't get up yet.
a2-imperativonegativo-04.canDo: I can place pronouns after affirmative commands (hazlo) and before negative commands (no lo hagas).

a2-imperativonegativo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Kitchen Rules
a2-imperativonegativo-05.scenario: A new guest at the hostel asks you about the house rules for the kitchen and the night.
a2-imperativonegativo-05.prompt: Politely tell the guest not to leave dirty dishes in the sink and to keep quiet after ten.
cues: Say what not to leave in the sink
Say when to keep quiet
a2-imperativonegativo-05.target: No deje platos sucios en el fregadero y guarde silencio después de las diez.
a2-imperativonegativo-05.english: Do not leave dirty dishes in the sink and keep quiet after ten.
a2-imperativonegativo-05.canDo: I can read and understand signs indicating rules, prohibitions, and hostel policies.

a2-imperativonegativo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: House Rules for Everyone
a2-imperativonegativo-consolidation.scenario: At the hostel the door bell rings. Carlos wants to open it, and some guests are making noise.
a2-imperativonegativo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos (tú) not to open the door to a stranger and tell the guests (ustedes) not to make noise.
cues: Tell Carlos not to open the door
Tell the guests politely not to make noise
a2-imperativonegativo-consolidation.target: Carlos, no abras la puerta a un desconocido. Señores, no hagan ruido, por favor.
a2-imperativonegativo-consolidation.english: Carlos, don't open the door to a stranger. Gentlemen, please don't make noise.
a2-imperativonegativo-consolidation.canDo: I can express prohibitions clearly and politely in Spanish.

a2-pronombrescliticos-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Your Spanish Teacher
a2-pronombrescliticos-01.scenario: You are having coffee with Meg by Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. She asks how your Spanish class went. Your teacher explained the lesson to you and sent you a message afterwards.
a2-pronombrescliticos-01.prompt: Tell Meg that your teacher explained the lesson to you and sent you a message.
cues: Say what the teacher explained to you
Say what she sent you afterwards
a2-pronombrescliticos-01.target: La profesora me explicó la lección y me mandó un mensaje.
a2-pronombrescliticos-01.english: The teacher explained the lesson to me and sent me a message.
a2-pronombrescliticos-01.canDo: I can identify who receives the action using indirect pronouns (me, te, le, nos, les).

a2-pronombrescliticos-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Flowers and a Letter
a2-pronombrescliticos-02.scenario: Carlos asks what you did yesterday. You bought some flowers and took them home, and you wrote a letter to your mother.
a2-pronombrescliticos-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that you bought flowers and took them home, and that you wrote to your mother.
cues: Say you bought flowers and took them home (use a pronoun for the flowers)
Say you wrote a letter to your mother (use a pronoun for her)
a2-pronombrescliticos-02.target: Compré flores y las llevé a casa. Le escribí una carta a mi madre.
a2-pronombrescliticos-02.english: I bought flowers and took them home. I wrote a letter to my mother.
a2-pronombrescliticos-02.canDo: I can choose the correct pronoun for the direct object (lo/la/los/las) vs. indirect object (le/les).

a2-pronombrescliticos-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Lending a Map
a2-pronombrescliticos-03.scenario: Meg is going to a new part of Hanoi and asks if she can borrow your map. You say yes and ask her to give it back tomorrow.
a2-pronombrescliticos-03.prompt: Tell Meg that you will lend her the map and that she can give it back to you tomorrow.
cues: Say you will lend her the map (use two pronouns)
Say she can give it back to you tomorrow (use two pronouns)
a2-pronombrescliticos-03.target: Sí, te lo presto y me lo das mañana.
a2-pronombrescliticos-03.english: Yes, I'll lend it to you and you give it back to me tomorrow.
a2-pronombrescliticos-03.canDo: I can order object pronouns with the person before the thing (me lo, te la, nos los).

a2-pronombrescliticos-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Report for the Boss
a2-pronombrescliticos-04.scenario: At the office in Hanoi, Carlos asks whether you gave the report to the boss. You gave it to him yesterday.
a2-pronombrescliticos-04.prompt: Tell Carlos that you handed the report to the boss yesterday, using se and a pronoun for the report.
cues: Say you handed the report over (se + a pronoun)
Say who got it and when
a2-pronombrescliticos-04.target: Sí, se lo entregué al jefe ayer.
a2-pronombrescliticos-04.english: Yes, I handed it to the boss yesterday.
a2-pronombrescliticos-04.canDo: I can change 'le lo' and 'les la' to 'se lo' and 'se la'.

a2-pronombrescliticos-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Meg's Lost Notes
a2-pronombrescliticos-05.scenario: Meg is worried about her history exam tomorrow because she has lost her notes. You found them at home and you have them in your backpack.
a2-pronombrescliticos-05.prompt: Tell Meg not to worry and that you are going to give her the notes right now.
cues: Tell her not to worry
Say you are going to give her the notes now (attach the pronouns)
a2-pronombrescliticos-05.target: No te preocupes, voy a dártelos ahora mismo.
a2-pronombrescliticos-05.english: Don't worry, I'm going to give them to you right now.
a2-pronombrescliticos-05.canDo: I can attach pronouns to the end of infinitives and gerunds.

a2-pronombrescliticos-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Notes and a Lesson
a2-pronombrescliticos-consolidation.scenario: At home in Hanoi, Carlos asks whether you gave Meg the notes for her exam. You gave them to her yesterday, and tomorrow you are going to explain the lesson to her.
a2-pronombrescliticos-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos that you gave Meg the notes yesterday and that tomorrow you are going to explain the lesson to her.
cues: Say you gave her the notes yesterday (se + a pronoun)
Say you are going to explain the lesson to her tomorrow (attach the pronouns)
a2-pronombrescliticos-consolidation.target: Sí, se los di ayer y mañana voy a explicársela.
a2-pronombrescliticos-consolidation.english: Yes, I gave them to her yesterday and tomorrow I'm going to explain it to her.
a2-pronombrescliticos-consolidation.canDo: I can use Spanish clitic pronouns accurately across statements, questions, and commands.

a2-condicionalsimple-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Life by the Sea
a2-condicionalsimple-01.scenario: At a café in Hanoi, Meg asks you about your dream life in the future. You would travel to Spain and live near the beach.
a2-condicionalsimple-01.prompt: Tell Meg that you would travel to Spain and live near the beach.
cues: Say where you would travel
Say where you would live
a2-condicionalsimple-01.target: Viajaría a España y viviría cerca de la playa.
a2-condicionalsimple-01.english: I would travel to Spain and live near the beach.
a2-condicionalsimple-01.canDo: I can conjugate regular verbs in the conditional simple.

a2-condicionalsimple-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Would You Do?
a2-condicionalsimple-02.scenario: Carlos made a mistake in a report at the office and asks what you would do in his place. You would tell the truth and be careful.
a2-condicionalsimple-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would say and how you would act in his place.
cues: Say what you would say
Say how you would act
a2-condicionalsimple-02.target: En tu lugar, yo diría la verdad y tendría cuidado.
a2-condicionalsimple-02.english: In your place, I would tell the truth and be careful.
a2-condicionalsimple-02.canDo: I can conjugate irregular conditional verbs: podría, tendría, haría, diría.

a2-condicionalsimple-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Coffee at the Café
a2-condicionalsimple-03.scenario: You and Meg sit down at a café in Hanoi and the waiter comes to your table.
a2-condicionalsimple-03.prompt: Politely ask the waiter to bring you the menu, and say what you would like to drink.
cues: Ask politely for the menu
Say you would like a coffee with milk
a2-condicionalsimple-03.target: ¿Podría traernos la carta, por favor? Me gustaría un café con leche.
a2-condicionalsimple-03.english: Could you bring us the menu, please? I would like a coffee with milk.
a2-condicionalsimple-03.canDo: I can ask for bills, rooms, and services politely using conditional phrases.

a2-condicionalsimple-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Advice for Meg
a2-condicionalsimple-04.scenario: Meg tells you she has had a headache all week and she is very tired. You are her friend and you give her advice.
a2-condicionalsimple-04.prompt: Give Meg two pieces of advice: one with deberías and one with yo que tú.
cues: Advise her to rest, using deberías
Say what you would do in her place, using yo que tú
a2-condicionalsimple-04.target: Deberías descansar más. Yo que tú iría al médico.
a2-condicionalsimple-04.english: You should rest more. If I were you, I would go to the doctor.
a2-condicionalsimple-04.canDo: I can advise a friend on health with deberías, yo que tú and sería mejor.

a2-condicionalsimple-05.title: Communicative Challenge: My Dream Trip
a2-condicionalsimple-05.scenario: Carlos asks you what your dream trip would be like. You would tour the mountains and the beach, and it would be an unforgettable experience.
a2-condicionalsimple-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would do on your dream trip and what it would be like.
cues: Say where you would travel
Say what the trip would be like
a2-condicionalsimple-05.target: Recorrería la montaña y la playa. Sería una experiencia inolvidable.
a2-condicionalsimple-05.english: I would tour the mountains and the beach. It would be an unforgettable experience.
a2-condicionalsimple-05.canDo: I can describe what my dream vacation would be like.

a2-condicionalsimple-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Map and a Rest
a2-condicionalsimple-consolidation.scenario: At a hotel in Hanoi, you want a map of the city. Meg looks tired after the trip.
a2-condicionalsimple-consolidation.prompt: Politely ask the receptionist for a city map, then advise Meg to rest a little.
cues: Ask politely for a map of the city
Advise Meg to rest, using deberías
a2-condicionalsimple-consolidation.target: Por favor, ¿tendría un mapa de la ciudad? Meg, deberías descansar un poco.
a2-condicionalsimple-consolidation.english: Please, would you have a map of the city? Meg, you should rest a little.
a2-condicionalsimple-consolidation.canDo: I can ask for favors and services with high politeness.

a2-subjuntivobasico-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Good Luck, Meg
a2-subjuntivobasico-01.scenario: Meg has an important history exam tomorrow and she is nervous. You are her friend and you want to encourage her.
a2-subjuntivobasico-01.prompt: Tell Meg that you hope she is calm and that she has a lot of luck.
cues: Say you hope she is calm
Say you hope she has a lot of luck
a2-subjuntivobasico-01.target: Espero que estés tranquila y que tengas mucha suerte.
a2-subjuntivobasico-01.english: I hope you are calm and that you have a lot of luck.
a2-subjuntivobasico-01.canDo: I can distinguish between facts (indicative) and wishes or subjectivity (subjunctive).

a2-subjuntivobasico-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Museum on Saturday
a2-subjuntivobasico-02.scenario: You and Carlos are planning Saturday afternoon in Hanoi. You would like to visit the museum, and you would like Carlos to come with you.
a2-subjuntivobasico-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that you want to go to the museum and that you want him to come with you.
cues: Say you want to go to the museum
Say you want Carlos to come with you
a2-subjuntivobasico-02.target: Quiero ir al museo y quiero que vengas conmigo.
a2-subjuntivobasico-02.english: I want to go to the museum and I want you to come with me.
a2-subjuntivobasico-02.canDo: I can choose between the infinitive (one subject) and the subjunctive (two subjects).

a2-subjuntivobasico-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Before Meg's Trip
a2-subjuntivobasico-03.scenario: Meg is going to Ho Chi Minh City tomorrow for her course and she asks you what she should do tonight. You tell her what is important and what is necessary.
a2-subjuntivobasico-03.prompt: Tell Meg that it is important to get up early and that it is necessary to take her book.
cues: Say it is important that she gets up early
Say it is necessary that she takes her book
a2-subjuntivobasico-03.target: Es importante que te levantes temprano y es necesario que lleves el libro.
a2-subjuntivobasico-03.english: It is important that you get up early and it is necessary that you take the book.
a2-subjuntivobasico-03.canDo: I can express necessity and importance using 'es necesario que' and 'es importante que'.

a2-subjuntivobasico-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Call Me When You Arrive
a2-subjuntivobasico-04.scenario: Your friend Meg is leaving for Ho Chi Minh City tomorrow. You work at an office in Hanoi and you cannot go to the airport with her.
a2-subjuntivobasico-04.prompt: Ask Meg to call you when she arrives at the hotel, and say you will call her when you leave work.
cues: Ask her to call you when she arrives at the hotel
Say you will call her when you leave work
a2-subjuntivobasico-04.target: Llámame cuando llegues al hotel. Yo te llamo cuando salga del trabajo.
a2-subjuntivobasico-04.english: Call me when you arrive at the hotel. I'll call you when I leave work.
a2-subjuntivobasico-04.canDo: I can use the subjunctive with 'cuando' when referring to future events.

a2-subjuntivobasico-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Farewell Dinner
a2-subjuntivobasico-05.scenario: At a farewell dinner in Hanoi, Meg is about to leave for a month's course in Ho Chi Minh City. You are one of her friends.
a2-subjuntivobasico-05.prompt: Tell Meg that you are sad she is leaving but glad she can study there.
cues: Say you are sad that she is leaving
Say you are glad that she can study there
a2-subjuntivobasico-05.target: Me da tristeza que te vayas, pero me alegra que puedas estudiar allí.
a2-subjuntivobasico-05.english: It makes me sad that you are leaving, but I'm glad you can study there.
a2-subjuntivobasico-05.canDo: I can express joy, sorrow, and empathy using 'me alegra que' and 'siento que'.

a2-subjuntivobasico-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Welcome Home, Meg
a2-subjuntivobasico-consolidation.scenario: Meg is back in Hanoi after a month in Ho Chi Minh City. She is very tired when she arrives at the flat and you are there to welcome her.
a2-subjuntivobasico-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that you are glad she is here and that it is important for her to rest a little.
cues: Say you are glad that she is here
Say it is important that she rests
a2-subjuntivobasico-consolidation.target: Me alegra que estés aquí. Es importante que descanses un poco.
a2-subjuntivobasico-consolidation.english: I'm glad you are here. It is important that you rest a little.
a2-subjuntivobasico-consolidation.canDo: I can understand and apply the core triggers of the Spanish subjunctive mood.

a2-perifrasisverbales-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Changed
a2-perifrasisverbales-01.scenario: At home in Hanoi, Meg asks what changed in your daily habits last year. You stopped eating bread and went back to cooking at home.
a2-perifrasisverbales-01.prompt: Tell Meg that you stopped eating bread and went back to cooking at home.
cues: Say you stopped eating bread
Say you went back to cooking at home
a2-perifrasisverbales-01.target: Dejé de comer pan y volví a cocinar en casa.
a2-perifrasisverbales-01.english: I stopped eating bread and went back to cooking at home.
a2-perifrasisverbales-01.canDo: I can explain when an action begins (empezó a llover), ends (dejó de fumar), or repeats (volví a llamar).

a2-perifrasisverbales-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Still the Same
a2-perifrasisverbales-02.scenario: Carlos calls you from his office in Hanoi and asks whether anything has changed. Nothing has: you are still studying Spanish and still living in the same house.
a2-perifrasisverbales-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that you are still studying Spanish and still living in the same house.
cues: Say you still study Spanish
Say you still live in the same house
a2-perifrasisverbales-02.target: Sigo estudiando español y sigo viviendo en la misma casa.
a2-perifrasisverbales-02.english: I'm still studying Spanish and I'm still living in the same house.
a2-perifrasisverbales-02.canDo: I can express continuous ongoing activities with 'seguir + gerundio'.

a2-perifrasisverbales-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Walk in the Heat
a2-perifrasisverbales-03.scenario: You and Meg are planning a walk around a lake in Hanoi. It is very hot, but you still want to go. Meg asks what you think.
a2-perifrasisverbales-03.prompt: Tell Meg that it is very hot, but that you want to go for a walk anyway.
cues: Say it is very hot
Add a contrast and say you want to go for a walk
a2-perifrasisverbales-03.target: Hace mucho calor; sin embargo, quiero dar un paseo.
a2-perifrasisverbales-03.english: It is very hot; however, I want to go for a walk.
a2-perifrasisverbales-03.canDo: I can link complex ideas with 'sin embargo', 'por lo tanto', 'además', and 'aunque'.

a2-perifrasisverbales-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Staying at the Café
a2-perifrasisverbales-04.scenario: You and Carlos are in a café in Hanoi when a heavy storm starts. Carlos asks if you want to leave.
a2-perifrasisverbales-04.prompt: Tell Carlos that, since it is raining a lot, the two of you are staying at the café.
cues: Give the reason with a 'since' connector
Say you are staying at the café
a2-perifrasisverbales-04.target: Ya que llueve mucho, nos quedamos en el café.
a2-perifrasisverbales-04.english: Since it is raining a lot, we are staying at the café.
a2-perifrasisverbales-04.canDo: I can explain causes using 'ya que' and 'puesto que'.

a2-perifrasisverbales-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting Used to Hanoi
a2-perifrasisverbales-05.scenario: At home in Hanoi, Meg asks how the beginning in the city was for you. At first it was hard, but little by little you got used to it.
a2-perifrasisverbales-05.prompt: Tell Meg that at first it was hard, but little by little you got used to Hanoi.
cues: Say that at first it was hard
Add that little by little you got used to the city
a2-perifrasisverbales-05.target: Al principio fue difícil; sin embargo, poco a poco me acostumbré a Hanói.
a2-perifrasisverbales-05.english: At first it was hard; however, little by little I got used to Hanoi.
a2-perifrasisverbales-05.canDo: I can tell how someone got used to a new place and changed their habits.

a2-perifrasisverbales-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My Routine Now
a2-perifrasisverbales-consolidation.scenario: Carlos asks you over dinner in Hanoi what has changed in your routine and what is still the same. You stopped having dinner late, but you still study Spanish even though it is difficult.
a2-perifrasisverbales-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos that you stopped having dinner late and that you still study Spanish although it is difficult.
cues: Say you stopped having dinner late
Say you still study Spanish
Add that it is difficult, with a contrast word
a2-perifrasisverbales-consolidation.target: Dejé de cenar tarde y sigo estudiando español, aunque es difícil.
a2-perifrasisverbales-consolidation.english: I stopped having dinner late and I still study Spanish, although it is difficult.
a2-perifrasisverbales-consolidation.canDo: I can narrate continuous actions and transitions in Spanish.

a2-educacionyestudios-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Favourite Subjects
a2-educacionyestudios-01.scenario: At home in Hanoi, Carlos asks you about school. Your favourite subject was literature, and languages come easily to you.
a2-educacionyestudios-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that your favourite subject at school was literature and that you are good at languages.
cues: Say your favourite subject at school was literature
Say you are good at languages
a2-educacionyestudios-01.target: Mi asignatura favorita era la literatura. Se me dan bien los idiomas.
a2-educacionyestudios-01.english: My favourite subject was literature. I'm good at languages.
a2-educacionyestudios-01.canDo: I can talk about my favorite school and university subjects in Spanish.

a2-educacionyestudios-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Meet at the Library
a2-educacionyestudios-02.scenario: Meg shows you her university in Hanoi. She asks where you two should meet after her class.
a2-educacionyestudios-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you will meet at the library after class.
cues: Say where to meet
Say when to meet
a2-educacionyestudios-02.target: Nos vemos en la biblioteca después de clase.
a2-educacionyestudios-02.english: We'll meet at the library after class.
a2-educacionyestudios-02.canDo: I can navigate a university campus in Spanish.

a2-educacionyestudios-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Midterm Result
a2-educacionyestudios-03.scenario: Carlos asks you how your history midterm went. You are happy: you passed with an outstanding grade.
a2-educacionyestudios-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you passed the history midterm with an outstanding grade.
cues: Say you passed the midterm
Say it was an outstanding grade
a2-educacionyestudios-03.target: Aprobé el examen parcial de historia con un sobresaliente.
a2-educacionyestudios-03.english: I passed the history midterm with an outstanding grade.
a2-educacionyestudios-03.canDo: I can talk about exam results in Spanish.

a2-educacionyestudios-04.title: Communicative Challenge: How I Prepare
a2-educacionyestudios-04.scenario: Carlos asks how you get ready before an exam. You underline the key ideas and write a summary in your notebook.
a2-educacionyestudios-04.prompt: Tell Carlos how you prepare for an exam: underline key ideas and write a summary.
cues: Say you underline the key ideas
Say you write a summary in your notebook
a2-educacionyestudios-04.target: Subrayo las ideas clave y escribo un resumen en mi libreta.
a2-educacionyestudios-04.english: I underline the key ideas and write a summary in my notebook.
a2-educacionyestudios-04.canDo: I can explain how I study and prepare for an exam.

a2-educacionyestudios-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Summer in Granada
a2-educacionyestudios-05.scenario: Meg tells you she has won a scholarship for a one-month summer course in Granada. You want to know where she will live.
a2-educacionyestudios-05.prompt: Tell Meg that this is great news and ask her whether she will live in a student residence.
cues: React happily to the news
Ask if she will live in a student residence
a2-educacionyestudios-05.target: ¡Qué bien, Meg! ¿Vas a vivir en una residencia de estudiantes?
a2-educacionyestudios-05.english: How great, Meg! Are you going to live in a student residence?
a2-educacionyestudios-05.canDo: I can express interest in international study programs in Spanish.

a2-educacionyestudios-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Studies and Me
a2-educacionyestudios-consolidation.scenario: Meg asks you about your studies. History is hard for you, languages come easily, and you write a summary of your notes.
a2-educacionyestudios-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that history is hard for you, that you are good at languages and that you make a summary of your notes.
cues: Say history is hard for you
Say you are good at languages
Say you make a summary of your notes
a2-educacionyestudios-consolidation.target: Me cuesta la historia, pero se me dan bien los idiomas. Hago un resumen de mis apuntes.
a2-educacionyestudios-consolidation.english: History is hard for me, but I'm good at languages. I make a summary of my notes.
a2-educacionyestudios-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about my subjects, exams and study methods in Spanish.

a2-porpara-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Spanish
a2-porpara-01.scenario: At home in Hanoi, Carlos asks why you study Spanish every day. You want to be able to talk with his grandmother in Madrid.
a2-porpara-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that you study Spanish to talk with his grandmother.
cues: Say you study Spanish
Give your purpose: talking with his grandmother
a2-porpara-01.target: Estudio español para hablar con tu abuela.
a2-porpara-01.english: I study Spanish to talk with your grandmother.
a2-porpara-01.canDo: I can use 'para' to express purpose and goals.

a2-porpara-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Stuck in Traffic
a2-porpara-02.scenario: You meet Meg at a café in Hanoi, half an hour late. The traffic was terrible and that is why you are late.
a2-porpara-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you were late because of the traffic.
cues: Say you were late
Give the reason: the traffic
a2-porpara-02.english: I was late because of the traffic.
a2-porpara-02.canDo: I can use 'por' to give reasons and causes.

a2-porpara-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Due Next Tuesday
a2-porpara-03.scenario: Meg asks you when your history assignment is due. It is due next Monday.
a2-porpara-03.prompt: Tell Meg that the history assignment is due next Monday.
cues: Say what is due
Give the deadline
a2-porpara-03.target: El trabajo de historia es para el próximo lunes.
a2-porpara-03.english: The history assignment is due next Monday.
a2-porpara-03.canDo: I can use 'para' for deadlines and cut-off dates.

a2-porpara-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Good Price
a2-porpara-04.scenario: Meg admires your new bicycle in Hanoi and asks how much it cost. You paid a hundred euros for it.
a2-porpara-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you paid a hundred euros for the bicycle.
cues: Say you paid
Give the price
a2-porpara-04.target: Pagué cien euros por la bicicleta.
a2-porpara-04.english: I paid a hundred euros for the bicycle.
a2-porpara-04.canDo: I can use 'por' for prices, sales, and exchanges.

a2-porpara-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Off to Madrid
a2-porpara-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks when you leave for Madrid and why you are going. You leave tomorrow morning to see your grandmother.
a2-porpara-05.prompt: Tell Meg that you leave for Madrid tomorrow morning to see your grandmother.
cues: Say where you are leaving for
Say when: tomorrow morning
Give the purpose of the trip
a2-porpara-05.target: Salgo para Madrid mañana por la mañana para ver a mi abuela.
a2-porpara-05.english: I leave for Madrid tomorrow morning to see my grandmother.
a2-porpara-05.canDo: I can contrast 'por' and 'para' confidently in full sentences.

a2-porpara-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Package for Madrid
a2-porpara-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the package on the table in your flat in Hanoi. It is for your grandmother in Madrid and you are sending it by mail.
a2-porpara-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that the package is for your grandmother and that you are sending it by mail.
cues: Say who the package is for
Say how you are sending it
a2-porpara-consolidation.target: Este paquete es para mi abuela y lo envío por correo.
a2-porpara-consolidation.english: This package is for my grandmother and I am sending it by mail.
a2-porpara-consolidation.canDo: I can confidently distinguish between por and para in everyday speech and writing.

a2-indefinidosnegacion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Nobody in the Kitchen
a2-indefinidosnegacion-01.scenario: You are staying at the home of Carlos's grandmother in Madrid. Carlos heard a noise in the kitchen and asks whether you saw anyone there. You saw no one.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that you did not see anyone in the kitchen.
cues: Say you did not see anyone
Say where: the kitchen
a2-indefinidosnegacion-01.target: No he visto a nadie en la cocina.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-01.english: I haven't seen anyone in the kitchen.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-01.canDo: I can ask whether someone is there and say that nobody is, using alguien and nadie.

a2-indefinidosnegacion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Nothing to Eat
a2-indefinidosnegacion-02.scenario: You are at the Madrid office where Carlos works for a few days. Carlos asks if you want something to eat before you leave. You want nothing, but you have some water.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that you don't want anything and that you have some water.
cues: Say you do not want anything
Say you have a little water
a2-indefinidosnegacion-02.target: No quiero nada, gracias. Tengo algo de agua.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-02.english: I don't want anything, thank you. I have some water.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-02.canDo: I can ask for something and say that I want nothing, using algo and nada.

a2-indefinidosnegacion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: No Plans for the Weekend
a2-indefinidosnegacion-03.scenario: Carlos's grandmother asks in Madrid whether you have any plan for the weekend. You have none, and you ask if she has one.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-03.prompt: Tell her you have no plan and ask whether she has one.
cues: Say you have no plan
Ask if she has a plan
a2-indefinidosnegacion-03.target: No tengo ningún plan para el fin de semana. ¿Tienes algún plan tú?
a2-indefinidosnegacion-03.english: I have no plan for the weekend. Do you have any plan?
a2-indefinidosnegacion-03.canDo: I can say that I have some or no plan, doubt or problem, using algún, alguna, ningún and ninguna.

a2-indefinidosnegacion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Neither Do I
a2-indefinidosnegacion-04.scenario: At dinner at the grandmother's home in Madrid, Carlos says that he doesn't like the cold. You don't like it either.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-04.prompt: Agree with Carlos and say you never go out without a jacket.
cues: Agree that you don't like it either
Say what you never do
a2-indefinidosnegacion-04.target: A mí tampoco me gusta el frío. Nunca salgo sin chaqueta.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-04.english: I don't like the cold either. I never go out without a jacket.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-04.canDo: I can agree with a negative sentence using tampoco and say what I never do using nunca.

a2-indefinidosnegacion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Nobody Told Me
a2-indefinidosnegacion-05.scenario: In the Madrid office, a colleague of Carlos asks you whether you know anything about tomorrow's meeting. Nobody told you anything.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-05.prompt: Tell the colleague that you don't know anything and that nobody told you about the meeting.
cues: Say you do not know anything
Say nobody told you about the meeting
a2-indefinidosnegacion-05.target: No sé nada. Nadie me dijo nada sobre la reunión.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-05.english: I don't know anything. Nobody told me anything about the meeting.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-05.canDo: I can combine nadie, nada, ningún, tampoco and nunca in short conversations.

a2-indefinidosnegacion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Quiet Day in Madrid
a2-indefinidosnegacion-consolidation.scenario: In the evening at the grandmother's home in Madrid, Carlos asks what you did today. You did nothing and saw nobody.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos that today you did nothing and saw nobody.
cues: Say you did nothing today
Say you saw nobody
a2-indefinidosnegacion-consolidation.target: Hoy no he hecho nada y no he visto a nadie.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-consolidation.english: Today I haven't done anything and I haven't seen anyone.
a2-indefinidosnegacion-consolidation.canDo: I can use indefinite and negative words to talk about people, things and time in everyday conversation.

a2-perifrasisduracion-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Just Bought
a2-perifrasisduracion-01.scenario: At Valencia station, Carlos asks whether you have already bought the tickets for the way back to Madrid. You bought them a moment ago.
a2-perifrasisduracion-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that you have just bought the tickets.
cues: Say you have just done it
Say what you bought
a2-perifrasisduracion-01.target: Acabo de comprar los boletos de vuelta.
a2-perifrasisduracion-01.english: I have just bought the tickets back.
a2-perifrasisduracion-01.canDo: I can say that something has just happened using acabar de + infinitive.

a2-perifrasisduracion-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Over a Year of Spanish
a2-perifrasisduracion-02.scenario: On the train from Madrid to Valencia, Meg asks Carlos how long he has been studying Spanish. It has been more than a year.
a2-perifrasisduracion-02.prompt: Tell Meg how long you have been studying Spanish.
cues: Say how long
Say what you have been doing
a2-perifrasisduracion-02.target: Llevo más de un año estudiando español.
a2-perifrasisduracion-02.english: I have been studying Spanish for more than a year.
a2-perifrasisduracion-02.canDo: I can say how long I have been doing something using llevar + time + gerund.

a2-perifrasisduracion-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Months Without My Mother
a2-perifrasisduracion-03.scenario: In Madrid, Carlos's grandmother asks when Carlos last saw his mother in Hungary. He has not seen her for three months.
a2-perifrasisduracion-03.prompt: Tell her how long you have not seen your mother.
cues: Say how long
Mention your mother
a2-perifrasisduracion-03.target: Llevo tres meses sin ver a mi madre.
a2-perifrasisduracion-03.english: I haven't seen my mother for three months.
a2-perifrasisduracion-03.canDo: I can say how long I have not done something using llevar + time + sin + infinitive.

a2-perifrasisduracion-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Rain in Valencia
a2-perifrasisduracion-04.scenario: In Valencia it starts to rain as you leave the station. Meg asks what you did when you saw the rain. You went into a café and had a coffee with milk.
a2-perifrasisduracion-04.prompt: Tell Meg what you did when you saw the rain.
cues: Say what you saw
Say where you went in
Say what you started to do
a2-perifrasisduracion-04.target: Al ver la lluvia, entramos en un café. Nos pusimos a tomar café con leche.
a2-perifrasisduracion-04.english: On seeing the rain, we went into a café. We started drinking coffee with milk.
a2-perifrasisduracion-04.canDo: I can say what I started to do with ponerse a and what happened on arriving with al + infinitive.

a2-perifrasisduracion-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Back from the Trip
a2-perifrasisduracion-05.scenario: Back in Madrid, Carlos's grandmother asks how you are after the trip. You have just arrived and you have not rested for two days.
a2-perifrasisduracion-05.prompt: Tell her that you have just arrived and that you have not rested for two days.
cues: Say you have just arrived
Say how long you have not rested
a2-perifrasisduracion-05.target: Acabamos de llegar y llevamos dos días sin descansar.
a2-perifrasisduracion-05.english: We have just arrived and we haven't rested for two days.
a2-perifrasisduracion-05.canDo: I can combine acabar de, llevar and al + infinitive to tell a short story.

a2-perifrasisduracion-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Whole Conversation
a2-perifrasisduracion-consolidation.scenario: At the grandmother's home in Madrid, she asks Meg how her Spanish is. Meg has been studying for more than a year and has just understood a whole conversation.
a2-perifrasisduracion-consolidation.prompt: Tell her how long you have been studying and what you have just understood.
cues: Say how long you have been studying
Say what you have just understood
a2-perifrasisduracion-consolidation.target: Llevo más de un año estudiando español y acabo de entender toda la conversación.
a2-perifrasisduracion-consolidation.english: I have been studying Spanish for more than a year and I have just understood the whole conversation.
a2-perifrasisduracion-consolidation.canDo: I can use acabar de, llevar + time, ponerse a and al + infinitive in everyday sentences.

a2-restaurant.title: Communicative Challenge: Dining Out
a2-restaurant.scenario: You are ordering dinner at a traditional restaurant for your table.
a2-restaurant.prompt: Order for the table: an appetizer, drinks, and a main course, and ask about the bill.
cues: 1. Request table/greeting: 'Buenas noches, una mesa para dos, por favor.'
2. Order drinks & appetizer: 'De primero queremos unas tapas y vino tinto.'
3. Order main: 'De segundo, el pescado del día.'
a2-restaurant.canDo: I can order a complete meal and drinks for a group in a restaurant.

a2-directions.title: Communicative Challenge: Finding Your Way
a2-directions.scenario: You are lost in the city center trying to find the train station.
a2-directions.prompt: Stop someone on the street, apologize for the interruption, ask where the train station is, and ask if it is far on foot.
cues: 1. Polite opening (Disculpe / Perdón)
2. Ask direction (¿Dónde está la estación de tren?)
3. Ask distance (¿Está lejos a pie?)
a2-directions.canDo: I can ask for and understand simple directions in town.

b1-story.title: Communicative Challenge: Recounting an Event
b1-story.scenario: A friend asks about an unusual experience you had recently.
b1-story.prompt: Describe an unexpected event that happened to you: where you were, what was happening, what suddenly occurred, and how it was resolved.
cues: Set background scene with imperfect tense
Narrate key actions with preterite tense
Express reaction or outcome
b1-story.canDo: I can describe past events, unexpected incidents, and personal reactions in connected speech.

b2-movie-review.title: Communicative Challenge: Film Analysis
b2-movie-review.scenario: You are contributing to a discussion group about cinema.
b2-movie-review.prompt: Describe the plot of the last movie or series you saw, analyze the main characters' motivations, and explain why you would or wouldn't recommend it.
cues: Premise & setting summary
Character dynamics and conflicts
Critical evaluation and recommendation
b2-movie-review.canDo: I can summarize plots, analyze character motivation, and critique films with reasoned arguments.

a1-01-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Morning Greeting
a1-01-01.scenario: You arrive at the language exchange in the morning and see Carlos at a table. He helps you with your Spanish, and then you need to leave; you will see him again tomorrow.
a1-01-01.prompt: Greet Carlos for the morning, thank him, and say see you tomorrow.
cues: Greet Carlos for the morning
Say thank you
Say see you tomorrow
a1-01-01.english: Good morning, Carlos. Thank you. See you tomorrow!
a1-01-01.canDo: I can greet someone in Spanish.

a1-01-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Introducing Yourself
a1-01-02.scenario: Meg sits down at your table at the language exchange and says she is a student. You are Carlos, and you are from Hungary.
a1-01-02.prompt: Say hello to Meg, tell her that you are Carlos, and say where you are from.
cues: Say hello to Meg
Say that you are Carlos
Say where you are from
a1-01-02.target: Hola, Meg. Soy Carlos. Soy de Hungría.
a1-01-02.english: Hello, Meg. I am Carlos. I am from Hungary.
a1-01-02.canDo: I can say my name in Spanish.

a1-01-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Asking Someone's Name
a1-01-03.scenario: It is the afternoon and you meet someone new at the language exchange. You are Meg and want to introduce yourself and learn the other person's name.
a1-01-03.prompt: Greet the person for the afternoon, say your name is Meg, and ask what their name is.
cues: Greet the person for the afternoon
Say your name is Meg
Ask what their name is
a1-01-03.target: Buenas tardes. Me llamo Meg. ¿Cómo te llamas?
a1-01-03.english: Good afternoon. My name is Meg. What is your name?
a1-01-03.canDo: I can ask someone their name.

a1-01-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Are You From?
a1-01-04.scenario: You are Carlos from Hungary, chatting with Meg at the language exchange. You want to tell her where you are from and ask where she is from.
a1-01-04.prompt: Say that you are Carlos, say you are from Hungary, and ask Meg where she is from.
cues: Say that you are Carlos
Say that you are from Hungary
Ask Meg where she is from
a1-01-04.target: Soy Carlos. Soy de Hungría. ¿De dónde eres, Meg?
a1-01-04.english: I am Carlos. I am from Hungary. Where are you from, Meg?
a1-01-04.canDo: I can say where I am from.

a1-01-05.title: Communicative Challenge: First Conversation
a1-01-05.scenario: Meg has just introduced herself to you at the Mexican restaurant in Hanoi. You are Carlos from Hungary and want to introduce yourself warmly and ask where she is from.
a1-01-05.prompt: Say your name is Carlos and that it is nice to meet Meg, say you are from Hungary, and ask where she is from.
cues: Say your name is Carlos and it is nice to meet Meg
Say that you are from Hungary
Ask where she is from
a1-01-05.target: Me llamo Carlos, mucho gusto, Meg. Soy de Hungría. ¿De dónde eres?
a1-01-05.english: My name is Carlos, nice to meet you, Meg. I am from Hungary. Where are you from?
a1-01-05.canDo: I can have a short first conversation.

a1-01-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Meeting at the Exchange
a1-01-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg at the evening language exchange. A new student sits down at your table and greets you.
a1-01-consolidation.prompt: Greet the student for the evening, say your name is Meg and that you are from South Africa, and ask what their name is.
cues: Greet the student for the evening
Say your name is Meg and that you are from South Africa
Ask what their name is
a1-01-consolidation.target: Buenas noches. Me llamo Meg y soy de Sudáfrica. ¿Cómo te llamas?
a1-01-consolidation.english: Good evening. My name is Meg and I am from South Africa. What is your name?
a1-01-consolidation.canDo: I can greet someone and respond appropriately.

a1-02-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Respond to an Introduction
a1-02-01.scenario: At the language exchange in Hanoi, Meg has just introduced you, Carlos, to her classmate. The classmate is waiting for you to say hello and say your name.
a1-02-01.prompt: Say hello, say your name is Carlos, and say you are pleased to meet her.
cues: Say hello
Say your name is Carlos
Say you are pleased to meet her
a1-02-01.english: Hello. My name is Carlos. Pleased to meet you.
a1-02-01.canDo: I can respond when someone introduces themselves.

a1-02-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Say Who Someone Is
a1-02-02.scenario: You are Meg at the language exchange in Hanoi. Carlos points at the woman at the next table and asks who she is. She is Daniela, a classmate of yours.
a1-02-02.prompt: Tell Carlos who the woman is and that she is your classmate.
cues: Say who she is
Say she is your classmate
a1-02-02.target: Ella es Daniela. Ella es mi compañera.
a1-02-02.english: She is Daniela. She is my classmate.
a1-02-02.canDo: I can say who a person is.

a1-02-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Ask Why
a1-02-03.scenario: You are Carlos at the language exchange in Hanoi. You are new there because you are a student, and you are chatting with Meg about her Spanish.
a1-02-03.prompt: Tell Meg you are new here because you are a student, and ask her why she studies Spanish.
cues: Say you are new here and give your reason
Ask Meg why she studies Spanish
a1-02-03.target: Soy nuevo aquí porque soy estudiante. ¿Por qué estudias español, Meg?
a1-02-03.english: I am new here because I am a student. Why do you study Spanish, Meg?
a1-02-03.canDo: I can ask a simple question with por qué.

a1-02-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Introduce Another Person
a1-02-04.scenario: You are Meg at the language exchange in Hanoi. Carlos has just sat down at your table, and your friend Daniela from class is next to you.
a1-02-04.prompt: Introduce Daniela to Carlos, say she is your friend, and say she is also your classmate.
cues: Introduce Daniela to Carlos
Say she is your friend
Say she is also your classmate
a1-02-04.target: Carlos, te presento a Daniela. Ella es mi amiga y también mi compañera.
a1-02-04.english: Carlos, let me introduce Daniela to you. She is my friend and also my classmate.

a1-02-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A First Conversation
a1-02-05.scenario: You are Meg at the language exchange in Hanoi. Your friend Daniela has joined the group, and Carlos is sitting between you. You want them to meet, and you are curious about Carlos.
a1-02-05.prompt: Introduce Carlos to Daniela as your friend, then ask Carlos why he studies Spanish.
cues: Introduce Carlos to Daniela as your friend
Ask Carlos why he studies Spanish
a1-02-05.target: Daniela, él es mi amigo Carlos. Carlos, ¿por qué estudias español?
a1-02-05.english: Daniela, he is my friend Carlos. Carlos, why do you study Spanish?
a1-02-05.canDo: I can introduce someone in a short conversation.

a1-02-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Meet Meg's Friend
a1-02-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos at the language exchange in Hanoi. Meg has just introduced you to her friend Daniela, who is waiting for your reply.
a1-02-consolidation.prompt: Tell Daniela you are pleased to meet her, say your name is Carlos, and say that Meg is your friend.
cues: Say you are pleased to meet Daniela
Say your name is Carlos
Say Meg is your friend
a1-02-consolidation.target: Mucho gusto, Daniela. Me llamo Carlos. Meg es mi amiga.
a1-02-consolidation.english: Nice to meet you, Daniela. My name is Carlos. Meg is my friend.
a1-02-consolidation.canDo: I can respond to an introduction and say who a friend is.

a1-03-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Name Two Things
a1-03-01.scenario: You are Meg at the study table in the library in Hanoi. Carlos holds up a book and then a photo, and asks you what each one is.
a1-03-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that one thing is a book and the other is a photo.
cues: Say what the first thing is
Say what the second thing is
a1-03-01.target: Es un libro. Es una foto.
a1-03-01.english: It is a book. It is a photo.
a1-03-01.canDo: I can name a person or thing with an indefinite article.

a1-03-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Boy or Girl
a1-03-02.scenario: You are Carlos at the study table in the library in Hanoi. Meg is looking at the photo of your family in Hungary and asks what the two people in the front are, a boy and a girl.
a1-03-02.prompt: Tell Meg that one person in the photo is a boy and the other is a girl.
cues: Say that one person is a boy
Say that the other is a girl
a1-03-02.target: Es un chico. Es una chica.
a1-03-02.english: He is a boy. She is a girl.
a1-03-02.canDo: I can recognise basic masculine and feminine nouns.

a1-03-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Is It?
a1-03-03.scenario: You are Carlos at the study table in the library in Hanoi. Meg asks you where the phone and the photos are, and you can see both.
a1-03-03.prompt: Tell Meg where the phone is and where the photos are.
cues: Say where the phone is
Say where the photos are
a1-03-03.target: El teléfono está aquí. Las fotos están aquí.
a1-03-03.english: The phone is here. The photos are here.
a1-03-03.canDo: I can use el, la, los and las with familiar nouns.

a1-03-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Describe a Brother and a Sister
a1-03-04.scenario: You are Carlos at the study table in the library in Hanoi. Meg is looking at the photo of your family in Hungary and asks what your brother and your sister are like.
a1-03-04.prompt: Tell Meg that your brother is tall and your sister is friendly.
cues: Say what the brother is like
Say what the sister is like
a1-03-04.target: Él es alto. Ella es simpática.
a1-03-04.english: He is tall. She is friendly.
a1-03-04.canDo: I can describe a person with a simple adjective.

a1-03-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Is Carlos?
a1-03-05.scenario: You are Meg at the study table in the library in Hanoi. Your friend Daniela comes over and asks you who Carlos is, the boy sitting beside you.
a1-03-05.prompt: Tell Daniela that he is a tall boy and that he is friendly.
cues: Say who he is and that he is tall
Say that he is friendly
a1-03-05.target: Es un chico alto. Es simpático.
a1-03-05.english: He is a tall boy. He is friendly.
a1-03-05.canDo: I can identify a person with an article and an adjective.

a1-03-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Things on the Table
a1-03-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg at the study table in the library in Hanoi. Carlos points at a phone, some photos and a book, and asks what they are.
a1-03-consolidation.prompt: Say that one thing is a phone, say that the others are some photos, and say that the book is small.
cues: Say what the first thing is
Say what the others are
Say what the book is like
a1-03-consolidation.target: Es un teléfono. Son unas fotos. El libro es pequeño.
a1-03-consolidation.english: It is a phone. They are some photos. The book is small.
a1-03-consolidation.canDo: I can choose the right article for a noun.

a1-03c-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Carlos Like?
a1-03c-01.scenario: You are at the language exchange in Hanoi. Meg sits down next to you and asks what your friend Carlos is like. You know him well.
a1-03c-01.prompt: Tell Meg that Carlos is tall and friendly.
cues: Say who you are talking about
Say he is tall
Say he is friendly
a1-03c-01.canDo: I can describe someone's appearance or personality.

a1-03c-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Meg's Sisters
a1-03c-02.scenario: Carlos is looking at photos of Meg's family at the language exchange. He asks you about Meg's two sisters, and you know them both: one is funny, the other is shy.
a1-03c-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that Lauren is funny and that Kaylee is shy.
cues: Say Lauren is funny
Say Kaylee is shy
a1-03c-02.target: Lauren es divertida. Kaylee es tímida.
a1-03c-02.english: Lauren is funny. Kaylee is shy.
a1-03c-02.canDo: I can recognise masculine and feminine adjective forms.

a1-03c-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Friends
a1-03c-03.scenario: At the language exchange in Hanoi, Meg asks you about two people in your class, Carlos and Daniela. You think they are both tall and friendly.
a1-03c-03.prompt: Tell Meg that Carlos and Daniela are tall and friendly.
cues: Name both people
Say they are tall
Say they are friendly
a1-03c-03.target: Carlos y Daniela son altos y simpáticos.
a1-03c-03.english: Carlos and Daniela are tall and friendly.
a1-03c-03.canDo: I can describe more than one person.

a1-03c-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Is Daniela?
a1-03c-04.scenario: A new student joins the group at the language exchange. Carlos points at Daniela and asks you who she is. She is a friendly woman and a teacher in your class.
a1-03c-04.prompt: Tell Carlos that Daniela is a friendly woman.
cues: Say her name
Say she is a woman
Say she is friendly
a1-03c-04.canDo: I can identify a person with a simple noun phrase.

a1-03c-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Is the Teacher?
a1-03c-05.scenario: You and Carlos are looking at a group photo from your class. Carlos asks who the man next to Daniela is. He is older and serious, and he is a teacher.
a1-03c-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that the man is older and serious, and that he is a teacher.
cues: Say he is a man
Say he is older and serious
Say he is a teacher
a1-03c-05.target: Es un hombre mayor y serio. Es profesor.
a1-03c-05.english: He is an older, serious man. He is a teacher.
a1-03c-05.canDo: I can describe a person with two or more adjectives.

a1-03c-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Introducing Carlos
a1-03c-consolidation.scenario: At the language exchange, Meg introduces you to her friend Daniela. Daniela has not met Carlos yet and asks who he is. You tell her about him: where he is from and what he is like.
a1-03c-consolidation.prompt: Tell Daniela that Carlos is a tall man and that he is from Hungary.
cues: Say Carlos is a man
Say he is tall
Say where he is from
a1-03c-consolidation.target: Carlos es un hombre alto. Es de Hungría.
a1-03c-consolidation.english: Carlos is a tall man. He is from Hungary.
a1-03c-consolidation.canDo: I can use un and una with words for people.

a1-05-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Brothers and Sisters
a1-05-01.scenario: You are chatting with Carlos at the language exchange in Hanoi. He asks whether you have brothers or sisters. You have one brother and one sister.
a1-05-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that you have a brother and a sister.
cues: Say you have a brother
Say you also have a sister
a1-05-01.target: Tengo un hermano y una hermana.
a1-05-01.english: I have a brother and a sister.
a1-05-01.canDo: I can use tener to say which family members you have.

a1-05-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Family Photo
a1-05-02.scenario: At the language exchange, Meg sees a photo on your phone of an older man and woman and asks who they are. They are your grandparents.
a1-05-02.prompt: Tell Meg that they are your grandparents.
cues: Say who they are
Say they are yours
a1-05-02.canDo: I can use mi, tu and su with singular and plural family nouns.

a1-05-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Cousins
a1-05-03.scenario: Carlos asks you about your cousins while you wait for the language exchange to start. You have two cousins, and your male cousin is very kind.
a1-05-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that you have two cousins and that your male cousin is kind.
cues: Say how many cousins you have
Say your male cousin is kind
a1-05-03.target: Tengo dos primos. Mi primo es amable.
a1-05-03.english: I have two cousins. My cousin is kind.
a1-05-03.canDo: I can talk about family relationships using tener and possessives.

a1-05-04.title: Communicative Challenge: My Parents
a1-05-04.scenario: Meg asks you what your parents are like while you have coffee after the language exchange. Your mother is calm and your father is kind.
a1-05-04.prompt: Tell Meg that your mother is calm and your father is kind.
cues: Say your mother is calm
Say your father is kind
a1-05-04.target: Mi madre es tranquila. Mi padre es amable.
a1-05-04.english: My mother is calm. My father is kind.
a1-05-04.canDo: I can describe family members with ser and simple adjectives.

a1-05-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Introducing My Sister
a1-05-05.scenario: You show Carlos a family photo on your phone at the language exchange. He asks who the girl next to you is. She is your sister, and she is funny.
a1-05-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that she is your sister and that she is funny.
cues: Say who she is
Say she is funny
a1-05-05.target: Ella es mi hermana. Es divertida.
a1-05-05.english: She is my sister. She is funny.
a1-05-05.canDo: I can introduce family members and give simple descriptions.

a1-05-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My Family
a1-05-consolidation.scenario: Meg asks about your family at the language exchange. You have a sister, and your mother is kind.
a1-05-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that you have a sister and that your mother is kind.
cues: Say you have a sister
Say your mother is kind
a1-05-consolidation.target: Tengo una hermana. Mi madre es amable.
a1-05-consolidation.english: I have a sister. My mother is kind.
a1-05-consolidation.canDo: I can retrieve family vocabulary and grammar.

a1-12-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Your age
a1-12-01.scenario: You are at the language exchange in Hanoi. Carlos asks how old you are. You are twenty.
a1-12-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how old you are.
cues: Say that you are twenty
Say it as an age, with the word for years
a1-12-01.canDo: Recognise and use Spanish numbers from 1 to 20.

a1-12-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How old is she?
a1-12-02.scenario: You are talking with Meg at the language exchange in Hanoi. She asks how old your grandmother is. She is seventy-five.
a1-12-02.prompt: Tell Meg how old your grandmother is.
cues: Mention your grandmother
Say that she is seventy-five years old
a1-12-02.target: Mi abuela tiene setenta y cinco años.
a1-12-02.english: My grandmother is seventy-five years old.
a1-12-02.canDo: Recognise and use numbers from 21 to 100.

a1-12-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What time is it?
a1-12-03.scenario: You are waiting outside the language school in Hanoi with Carlos. He asks you what time it is. It is half past four.
cues: Say what time it is
Include the half hour

a1-12-04.title: Communicative Challenge: When is the class?
a1-12-04.scenario: Carlos has invited you to his Spanish class in Hanoi. You want to know when it starts.
a1-12-04.prompt: Ask Carlos what time the class is.
cues: Ask what time something is
Mention the class
a1-12-04.canDo: Ask when and at what time something is.

a1-12-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Your evening
a1-12-05.scenario: Meg asks about your evening in Hanoi. You have class at six and dinner is at seven.
cues: Say you have class and when
Say when dinner is
a1-12-05.target: Tengo clase a las seis. La cena es a las siete.
a1-12-05.english: I have class at six. Dinner is at seven.
a1-12-05.canDo: Talk about a simple daily schedule.

a1-12-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My brother's day
a1-12-consolidation.scenario: Meg asks you about your younger brother in Hanoi: how old he is and what time his class is. He is twelve and his class is at eight.
a1-12-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg his age and when his class is.
cues: Say how old your brother is
Say what time he has class
a1-12-consolidation.target: Mi hermano tiene doce años. Tiene clase a las ocho.
a1-12-consolidation.english: My brother is twelve years old. He has class at eight.
a1-12-consolidation.canDo: I can use numbers, tell the time and talk about schedules.

a1-06-01.title: Communicative Challenge: My Day
a1-06-01.scenario: Carlos asks what you do on a normal day at the language exchange in Hanoi. You work in the morning and study Spanish in the afternoon.
a1-06-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that you work in the morning and study Spanish in the afternoon.
cues: Say what you do in the morning
Say what you do in the afternoon
a1-06-01.target: Trabajo por la mañana. Estudio español por la tarde.
a1-06-01.english: I work in the morning. I study Spanish in the afternoon.
a1-06-01.canDo: Say what I do using simple regular present-tense forms.

a1-06-02.title: Communicative Challenge: After Class
a1-06-02.scenario: Meg asks what you and Carlos do at home after class. You cook at home, and Carlos listens to music.
a1-06-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you cook at home and that Carlos listens to music.
cues: Say what you do at home
Say what Carlos does
a1-06-02.target: Cocino en casa. Carlos escucha música.
a1-06-02.english: I cook at home. Carlos listens to music.
a1-06-02.canDo: Use regular -ar verbs in the present tense.

a1-06-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Where I Live
a1-06-03.scenario: Daniela asks you where you live and what you drink in the morning. You live in Hanoi and you drink coffee.
a1-06-03.prompt: Tell Daniela where you live and what you drink in the morning.
cues: Say where you live
Say what you drink in the morning
a1-06-03.target: Vivo en Hanoi. Bebo café por la mañana.
a1-06-03.english: I live in Hanoi. I drink coffee in the morning.
a1-06-03.canDo: Use regular -er and -ir verbs in the present tense.

a1-06-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting Ready
a1-06-04.scenario: Meg asks you about your morning before the Spanish class in Hanoi. You get up early and you take a shower.
a1-06-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you get up early and that you take a shower in the morning.
cues: Say you get up early
Say you take a shower in the morning
a1-06-04.target: Me levanto temprano. Me ducho por la mañana.
a1-06-04.english: I get up early. I take a shower in the morning.
a1-06-04.canDo: Talk about my daily routine using reflexive verbs.

a1-06-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Full Day
a1-06-05.scenario: On Wednesday evening Carlos calls you on video and asks about your day. You get up and have breakfast, then you work, and after dinner you take a shower.
a1-06-05.prompt: Tell Carlos about your day: what you do first, then what you do next, and what you do after dinner.
cues: Say you get up and have breakfast
Say you work afterwards
Say what you do after dinner
a1-06-05.target: Me levanto y desayuno. Luego trabajo. Después de cenar me ducho.
a1-06-05.english: I get up and have breakfast. Then I work. After dinner I take a shower.
a1-06-05.canDo: Describe a full day with regular and reflexive verbs.

a1-06-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My Sister and My Day
a1-06-consolidation.scenario: Meg asks whether you have brothers or sisters. You have one sister, she is kind, and she works in the morning.
a1-06-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that you have a sister, that she is kind and that she works in the morning.
cues: Say you have a sister
Say she is kind
Say when she works
a1-06-consolidation.target: Tengo una hermana. Mi hermana es amable y trabaja por la mañana.
a1-06-consolidation.english: I have a sister. My sister is kind and she works in the morning.
a1-06-consolidation.canDo: I can use regular present tense, ser, and tener with earlier A1 vocabulary.

a1-reflexive-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Morning Wash
a1-reflexive-01.scenario: Meg asks about your morning before the Spanish class in Hanoi. You get up early, and you wash your face and brush your teeth.
a1-reflexive-01.prompt: Tell Meg that you get up early and that you wash your face and brush your teeth.
cues: Say you get up early
Say you wash your face and your teeth
a1-reflexive-01.target: Me levanto temprano y me lavo la cara y los dientes.
a1-reflexive-01.english: I get up early and I wash my face and brush my teeth.
a1-reflexive-01.canDo: Use reflexive pronouns to talk about getting up, showering and washing.

a1-reflexive-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Early and Late
a1-reflexive-02.scenario: Carlos asks when you wake up and when you go to bed. You wake up early and you go to bed late.
a1-reflexive-02.prompt: Tell Carlos that you wake up early and that you go to bed late.
cues: Say you wake up early
Say you go to bed late
a1-reflexive-02.target: Me despierto temprano y me acuesto tarde.
a1-reflexive-02.english: I wake up early and I go to bed late.
a1-reflexive-02.canDo: I can conjugate despertarse and acostarse with the correct vowel changes.

a1-reflexive-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Put On
a1-reflexive-03.scenario: Daniela asks what you do after you wake up on a school day. You get dressed and you put on a shirt and trousers.
a1-reflexive-03.prompt: Tell Daniela that you get dressed and that you put on a shirt and trousers.
cues: Say you get dressed
Say what you put on
a1-reflexive-03.target: Me visto y me pongo la camisa y los pantalones.
a1-reflexive-03.english: I get dressed and I put on the shirt and the trousers.
a1-reflexive-03.canDo: I can describe what I put on and wear each morning.

a1-reflexive-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Dishes and Hands
a1-reflexive-04.scenario: Carlos asks what you do after dinner. You wash the dishes and then you wash your hands.
a1-reflexive-04.prompt: Tell Carlos that you wash the dishes and that you wash your hands.
cues: Say you wash the dishes
Say you wash your hands
a1-reflexive-04.target: Lavo los platos y me lavo las manos.
a1-reflexive-04.english: I wash the dishes and I wash my hands.
a1-reflexive-04.canDo: Tell actions done to myself (me lavo) from actions done to something else (lavo).

a1-reflexive-05.title: Communicative Challenge: My Evening in Order
a1-reflexive-05.scenario: Meg asks you to tell your evening in order. You have dinner, then you brush your teeth, and before going to bed you read a book.
a1-reflexive-05.prompt: Tell Meg your evening in order: first dinner, then your teeth, and what you do before going to bed.
cues: Say what you do first
Say what you do next
Say what you do before going to bed
a1-reflexive-05.target: Primero ceno. Luego me lavo los dientes y, antes de acostarme, leo un libro.
a1-reflexive-05.english: First I have dinner. Then I brush my teeth and, before going to bed, I read a book.
a1-reflexive-05.canDo: I can narrate my full day step-by-step using sequence connectors.

a1-reflexive-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Mornings with My Sister
a1-reflexive-consolidation.scenario: Daniela asks about your mornings. You wake up early, and you and your sister take a shower in the morning.
a1-reflexive-consolidation.prompt: Tell Daniela that you wake up early and that you and your sister take a shower in the morning.
cues: Say you wake up early
Say you and your sister shower in the morning
a1-reflexive-consolidation.target: Me despierto temprano. Mi hermana y yo nos duchamos por la mañana.
a1-reflexive-consolidation.english: I wake up early. My sister and I take a shower in the morning.
a1-reflexive-consolidation.canDo: I can conjugate reflexive verbs correctly with all pronouns (me, te, se, nos, se).

a1-07-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Rooms in My Home
a1-07-01.scenario: Meg asks what rooms there are in your home. There is a kitchen, a bathroom and a garden.
a1-07-01.prompt: Tell Meg which rooms there are in your home: a kitchen, a bathroom and a garden.
cues: Say there is a kitchen
Say there is a bathroom
Say there is a garden
a1-07-01.target: Hay una cocina, un baño y un jardín.
a1-07-01.english: There is a kitchen, a bathroom and a garden.
a1-07-01.canDo: Identify and name the main rooms in a home.

a1-07-02.title: Communicative Challenge: In the Living Room
