b1-05-05.target: Meg March y Jo discutieron después de un malentendido. Su madre les aconsejó hablar tranquilamente y después se reconciliaron.
b1-05-05.english: Meg March and Jo argued after a misunderstanding. Their mother advised them to talk calmly and afterwards they made up.
b1-05-05.canDo: I can describe a difficult relationship using several structures.

b1-05-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Then and Now
b1-05-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how your relationship with your sister Kaylee was when you were small and how it is now.
b1-05-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos how you and Kaylee were before and how you are now.
cues: Say what you used to do when you were small
Say what has changed
Say what you do now
b1-05-consolidation.target: Cuando éramos pequeñas, Kaylee y yo solíamos discutir. Ahora nos hemos acercado y confiamos más la una en la otra.
b1-05-consolidation.english: When we were small, Kaylee and I used to argue. Now we have become closer and we trust each other more.
b1-05-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate relationships, habits, change and description.

b1-06-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Do at Work
b1-06-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your job in Budapest. You work in an office, you are responsible for coordinating a small team, and you have five years of experience.
b1-06-01.prompt: Tell Meg where you work, what you are responsible for and how much experience you have.
cues: Say where you work
Say what you are responsible for
Say how much experience you have
b1-06-01.target: Trabajo en una oficina y soy responsable de coordinar un equipo pequeño. Tengo cinco años de experiencia.
b1-06-01.english: I work in an office and I am responsible for coordinating a small team. I have five years of experience.
b1-06-01.canDo: I can describe a professional role using the present tense.

b1-06-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Before and Now
b1-06-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether your work is different from before. You used to work for a small company, and now your position has more responsibilities.
b1-06-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you used to do and how your position is different now.
cues: Say where you used to work
Say what is different now
b1-06-02.target: Antes trabajaba en una empresa pequeña, pero ahora tengo un puesto con más responsabilidades.
b1-06-02.english: I used to work for a small company, but now I have a position with more responsibilities.
b1-06-02.canDo: I can contrast former and current professional situations.

b1-06-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Job Advert
b1-06-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is looking for work and asks what the advert you found says. A person with experience is wanted, a good level of English is required, and working from home two days a week is permitted.
b1-06-03.prompt: Tell Meg what the advert says about the person, the English and working from home.
cues: Say who is wanted
Say what level of English is required
Say when working from home is permitted
b1-06-03.target: Se busca una persona con experiencia. Se requiere buen nivel de inglés y se permite trabajar desde casa dos días a la semana.
b1-06-03.english: A person with experience is wanted. A good level of English is required and working from home two days a week is permitted.
b1-06-03.canDo: I can describe workplace rules and processes impersonally.

b1-06-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Problem at the Office
b1-06-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You come home late and Meg asks what happened at the office. There was an error in a report, so your team had to repeat the analysis, and that caused a delay.
b1-06-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the error was and what the team had to do because of it.
cues: Say the cause of the problem
Say what you had to do
Say what the result was
b1-06-04.target: Debido a un error en el informe, tuvimos que repetir el análisis. Por eso hubo un retraso.
b1-06-04.english: Because of an error in the report, we had to repeat the analysis. So there was a delay.
b1-06-04.canDo: I can explain workplace problems through cause and consequence.

b1-06-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Story of Bartleby
b1-06-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have just read the story of Bartleby, and Carlos asks what happens in it. The copyist rejects the tasks, there are many delays, and in the end the lawyer moves his office to another building.
b1-06-05.prompt: Retell the story of Bartleby to Carlos in two sentences.
cues: Say who Bartleby is and what he does
Say what the lawyer does in the end
b1-06-05.target: Bartleby es un copista, pero rechaza las tareas y hay muchos retrasos. Al final, el abogado cambia su oficina a otro edificio.
b1-06-05.english: Bartleby is a copyist, but he rejects the tasks and there are many delays. In the end, the lawyer moves his office to another building.
b1-06-05.canDo: I can communicate professionally about requests and limitations.

b1-06-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Request You Cannot Accept
b1-06-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is helping you practise what to say at work tomorrow. A client will ask you to deliver the report tomorrow, but you have to finish another project first.
b1-06-consolidation.prompt: Tell the client you understand the request, but refuse politely, give your reason and ask for a new deadline.
cues: Say you understand the request
Refuse and give your reason
Ask for a new deadline
b1-06-consolidation.target: Entiendo la petición, pero no puedo entregar el informe mañana porque tengo que terminar otro proyecto. Necesito aclarar un nuevo plazo.
b1-06-consolidation.english: I understand the request, but I cannot deliver the report tomorrow because I have to finish another project. I need to clarify a new deadline.
b1-06-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about work, obligation, refusal and explanation in a professional setting.

b1-07-01.title: Communicative Challenge: How I Used to Study
b1-07-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you studied when you were a student at school. You used to study a lot before exams, and last year you passed a difficult subject at university.
b1-07-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how you used to study and what you passed last year.
cues: Say what you used to do before exams
Say what you passed last year
b1-07-01.target: Cuando era estudiante, estudiaba mucho antes de los exámenes. El año pasado aprobé una asignatura difícil.
b1-07-01.english: When I was a student, I used to study a lot before exams. Last year I passed a difficult subject.
b1-07-01.canDo: I can describe past learning experiences clearly.

b1-07-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How We Learn
b1-07-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how to learn Spanish well. You tell her that a lot is learned through practice and that you have to concentrate during the class.
b1-07-02.prompt: Tell Meg two general things about learning, without naming a person.
cues: Say what is learned through practice
Say what you have to do in class
b1-07-02.target: Se aprende mucho con la práctica. Hay que concentrarse durante la clase.
b1-07-02.english: A lot is learned through practice. You have to concentrate during the lesson.
b1-07-02.canDo: I can describe learning processes impersonally.

b1-07-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Studying in a Group
b1-07-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about studying in a group. You think it is useful, but you do not think that studying alone is always better.
b1-07-03.prompt: Tell Carlos your opinion about studying in a group and about studying alone.
cues: Say what you think about studying in a group
Say what you do not think about studying alone
b1-07-03.target: Creo que estudiar en grupo es útil, pero no creo que estudiar solo sea siempre mejor.
b1-07-03.english: I think studying in a group is useful, but I don't think studying alone is always better.
b1-07-03.canDo: I can express opinions with the indicative or subjunctive as appropriate.

b1-07-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Best Way to Learn
b1-07-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks which way of learning is better. For you, practice is more effective than memorising lists, and practising with other people is the best option.
b1-07-04.prompt: Compare practice with memorising lists and say what is the best option for you.
cues: Compare practice and memorising
Say what the best option is for you
b1-07-04.target: La práctica es más eficaz que memorizar listas. Para mí, practicar con otras personas es la mejor opción.
b1-07-04.english: Practice is more effective than memorising lists. For me, practising with other people is the best option.

b1-07-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Rousseau and Emilio
b1-07-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have just read about Rousseau and his book Emilio, and Carlos asks what Rousseau thinks about learning. For Rousseau, a child learns from experience and not only by memorising, and the teacher prepares situations.
b1-07-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Rousseau says about how a child learns and what the teacher does.
cues: Say how the child learns
Say what the teacher does
b1-07-05.target: Según Rousseau, el niño aprende con la experiencia y no solo memorizando. El profesor prepara situaciones para que el niño descubra.
b1-07-05.english: According to Rousseau, the child learns from experience and not only by memorising. The teacher prepares situations so that the child discovers.
b1-07-05.canDo: I can state and defend an opinion about education.

b1-07-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My Opinion on Learning
b1-07-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think is the best way to learn. You think practice is more effective than memorising lists, because it allows you to apply what you have learned.
b1-07-consolidation.prompt: Give your opinion, compare two methods and give a reason.
cues: Give your opinion
Compare practice and memorising
Give a reason
b1-07-consolidation.target: Creo que la práctica es más eficaz que memorizar listas porque permite aplicar lo aprendido.
b1-07-consolidation.english: I think practice is more effective than memorising lists because it allows you to apply what you have learned.
b1-07-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about education and learning, give opinions and compare methods.

b1-08-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Planning the Journey
b1-08-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip from Budapest to Madrid to see your grandmother. Meg asks what you are going to do first. You are going to prepare the itinerary tonight and look for accommodation.
b1-08-01.prompt: Tell Meg what you are going to do tonight and what you are going to look for.
cues: Say what you are going to prepare tonight
Say what you are going to look for
b1-08-01.target: Voy a preparar el itinerario esta noche y vamos a buscar un alojamiento.
b1-08-01.english: I am going to prepare the itinerary tonight and we are going to look for accommodation.
b1-08-01.canDo: I can explain a travel plan using future and intention structures.

b1-08-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Something Went Wrong
b1-08-02.scenario: You are Meg. You have just come back from Madrid and Carlos asks what happened at the station. When you arrived there were a lot of people, and the train left late because there was a breakdown.
b1-08-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the station was like when you arrived and why the train was late.
cues: Say what there was at the station
Say why the train left late
b1-08-02.target: Cuando llegamos a la estación, había mucha gente. El tren salió con retraso porque había una avería.
b1-08-02.english: When we arrived at the station, there were a lot of people. The train left late because there was a breakdown.
b1-08-02.canDo: I can narrate a travel problem using the main past tenses.

b1-08-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting Around Madrid
b1-08-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how you moved around Madrid on your first day. You travelled from the hotel to the station on foot and walked through the old town.
b1-08-03.prompt: Tell Meg where you travelled from and to, and where you walked.
cues: Say where you travelled from and to
Say where you walked
b1-08-03.target: Nos desplazamos desde el hotel hasta la estación y caminamos por el casco antiguo.
b1-08-03.english: We travelled from the hotel to the station and walked through the old town.
b1-08-03.canDo: I can describe movement through and between places.

b1-08-04.title: Communicative Challenge: If We Miss the Train
b1-08-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you will do if you miss the train in Madrid. You will look for an alternative and tell the accommodation.
b1-08-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what you will do if you miss the train.
cues: Say the condition
Say what you will do
b1-08-04.target: Si perdemos el tren, buscaremos una alternativa y avisaremos al alojamiento.
b1-08-04.english: If we miss the train, we will look for an alternative and notify the accommodation.
b1-08-04.canDo: I can discuss realistic travel contingencies.

b1-08-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Journey of Odiseo
b1-08-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have just read the story of Odiseo and Carlos asks what happens in it. A storm changes the course of his ships, he loses his ships and his men, and in the end he reaches Ítaca, where Penélope is waiting for him.
b1-08-05.prompt: Retell the story of Odiseo to Carlos in two sentences.
cues: Say what the storm does
Say how the journey ends
b1-08-05.target: Una tormenta cambia el rumbo de Odiseo y él pierde sus barcos. Al final llega a Ítaca, donde Penélope lo espera.
b1-08-05.english: A storm changes Odiseo's course and he loses his ships. In the end he reaches Ítaca, where Penélope is waiting for him.
b1-08-05.canDo: I can communicate about a journey using connected travel language.

b1-08-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Trip Plans and Problems
b1-08-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the trip to Madrid. You are going to travel by train, and if you miss the connection you will look for an alternative.
b1-08-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg your travel plan and what you will do if there is a problem.
cues: Say how you are going to travel
Say what you will do if you miss the connection
b1-08-consolidation.target: Vamos a viajar en tren. Si perdemos la conexión, buscaremos una alternativa.
b1-08-consolidation.english: We are going to travel by train. If we miss the connection, we will look for an alternative.
b1-08-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about travel plans, problems, routes and possible changes.

b1-09-01.title: Communicative Challenge: How Do You Feel?
b1-09-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos comes home from the office and asks how you are. You have felt dizzy since this morning, but you felt worse yesterday.
b1-09-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how you feel today and how you felt yesterday.
cues: Say how you feel today
Compare it with yesterday
b1-09-01.target: Me siento mareada desde esta mañana, aunque ayer me sentía peor.
b1-09-01.english: I have felt dizzy since this morning, although yesterday I felt worse.
b1-09-01.canDo: I can describe physical and emotional states with estar and sentirse.

b1-09-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Advice for a Tired Friend
b1-09-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg has felt exhausted for three days. You want to help her.
b1-09-02.prompt: Advise Meg to rest and to make a doctor's appointment.
cues: Recommend that she rests
Recommend that she makes an appointment
b1-09-02.target: Te recomiendo que descanses unos días y que pidas una consulta.
b1-09-02.english: I recommend that you rest for a few days and make an appointment.
b1-09-02.canDo: I can give health advice using the present subjunctive.

b1-09-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Healthy Habits
b1-09-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you do to sleep better after long days at the office. You walk after dinner and keep your phone away before bed.
b1-09-03.prompt: Tell Meg what you usually do and why.
cues: Say what you usually do after dinner
Say what you avoid before bed
Give a reason
b1-09-03.target: Suelo caminar después de cenar y evito el teléfono antes de acostarme, porque así duermo mejor.
b1-09-03.english: I usually walk after dinner and avoid the phone before going to bed, because that way I sleep better.
b1-09-03.canDo: I can describe regular health habits and routines.

b1-09-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Notice at the Clinic
b1-09-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the clinic near your flat in Budapest offers. You have read the notice on the door.
b1-09-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what is offered and what the notice recommends.
cues: Say what is offered on Fridays
Say what is recommended
b1-09-04.target: En esta clínica se ofrecen consultas gratuitas los viernes y se recomienda dormir bien.
b1-09-04.english: Free consultations are offered at this clinic on Fridays and it is recommended to sleep well.
b1-09-04.canDo: I can give general health information without naming an agent.

b1-09-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Gregor's Story
b1-09-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have read the story of Gregor, who wakes up one morning as an insect. Tell Carlos what happened and what you think about it.
b1-09-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Gregor found out and give your advice.
cues: Say what Gregor found out
Give advice and explain why it matters
b1-09-05.target: Una mañana, Gregor descubrió que ya no era una persona. Es importante que una persona descanse, y él nunca había tenido tiempo para hacerlo.
b1-09-05.english: One morning, Gregor found out that he was no longer a person. It is important that a person rests, and he had never had time to do it.
b1-09-05.canDo: I can give connected health advice and explain why it matters.

b1-09-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Asking for Advice
b1-09-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You feel exhausted and you usually sleep little. You ask Meg for advice.
b1-09-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how you feel, what you usually do, and ask what she recommends.
cues: Say how you feel
Say what you usually do
Ask for a recommendation
b1-09-consolidation.target: Me siento agotado y suelo dormir poco. ¿Qué me recomiendas que haga?
b1-09-consolidation.english: I feel exhausted and I usually sleep little. What do you recommend that I do?
b1-09-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate health and wellbeing language.

b1-10-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Where We Live
b1-10-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you to describe the flat you rent in Budapest and the area around it.
b1-10-01.prompt: Tell Meg where the flat is and what the neighbourhood is like.
cues: Say where the flat is
Describe the neighbourhood
b1-10-01.target: Vivimos en un piso que está cerca del centro. El barrio donde vivimos es bastante tranquilo.
b1-10-01.english: We live in a flat that is near the centre. The neighbourhood where we live is quite quiet.
b1-10-01.canDo: I can describe where I live using relative clauses.

b1-10-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Flats
b1-10-02.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are comparing two flats in Budapest. The second one is brighter, but the rent is high.
b1-10-02.prompt: Tell Carlos which flat is brighter and what is wrong with the rent.
cues: Compare the two flats
Say what you think of the rent
b1-10-02.target: Este piso es más luminoso que el otro, aunque el alquiler es demasiado alto.
b1-10-02.english: This flat is brighter than the other, although the rent is too high.
b1-10-02.canDo: I can compare different housing options.

b1-10-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Pipe Breaks
b1-10-03.scenario: You are Carlos. A pipe broke in the kitchen while you and Meg were sleeping. Your colleague at the office asks what happened.
b1-10-03.prompt: Tell what happened and what you did.
cues: Say what you were doing
Say what broke
Say what you did next
b1-10-03.target: Mientras dormíamos, una tubería se rompió, así que llamamos al propietario.
b1-10-03.english: While we were sleeping, a pipe broke, so we called the landlord.
b1-10-03.canDo: I can narrate a household problem clearly.

b1-10-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Would You Change?
b1-10-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you would change in your flat if you could.
b1-10-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would do and why.
cues: Say what you would enlarge or renovate
Give a reason
b1-10-04.target: Si pudiera, ampliaría la sala porque necesito más espacio.
b1-10-04.english: If I could, I would enlarge the living room because I need more space.
b1-10-04.canDo: I can discuss hypothetical changes to a home.

b1-10-05.title: Communicative Challenge: An Imperfect Flat
b1-10-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read a story about a narrator whose flat was worse than the advert. Tell Meg about it and say what home you would prefer.
b1-10-05.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to the narrator and what kind of home you would prefer.
cues: Say what the flat was like in the photos
Say what the narrator found
Say what home you would prefer
b1-10-05.target: El piso parecía perfecto en las fotos, pero era más pequeño. Yo preferiría una vivienda funcional y tranquila.
b1-10-05.english: The flat looked perfect in the photos, but it was smaller. I would prefer a functional, quiet home.
b1-10-05.canDo: I can describe and evaluate an ideal home.

b1-10-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: My Perfect Home
b1-10-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what kind of home you would like in Budapest.
b1-10-consolidation.prompt: Describe your perfect home and say why.
cues: Say what it would be like
Compare it with your flat
Give a reason
b1-10-consolidation.target: Mi vivienda perfecta sería más luminosa que este piso y tendría bastante privacidad porque necesito trabajar.
b1-10-consolidation.english: My ideal home would be brighter than this flat and would have enough privacy because I need to work.
b1-10-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate housing and description language.

b1-11-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Our Neighbourhood
b1-11-01.scenario: You are Meg. You are on the phone with Carlos's grandmother in Madrid. She asks what your neighbourhood in Budapest is like.
b1-11-01.prompt: Tell her about the neighbourhood and your street.
cues: Describe the neighbourhood
Say where your street is
b1-11-01.target: Vivimos en un barrio que tiene una plaza tranquila. La calle donde vivimos está cerca de una estación.
b1-11-01.english: We live in a neighbourhood that has a quiet square. The street where we live is near a station.
b1-11-01.canDo: I can describe my neighbourhood using relative clauses and location language.

b1-11-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Changing Area
b1-11-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the area of Madrid where your grandmother lives. You remember that there used to be less traffic, but the area has grown.
b1-11-02.prompt: Tell Meg how the area was before and how it has changed.
cues: Say what there used to be
Say what has changed since then
b1-11-02.target: Antes había menos tráfico, pero el barrio ha crecido mucho y, desde entonces, hay más servicios.
b1-11-02.english: There used to be less traffic, but the neighbourhood has grown a lot and, since then, there are more services.
b1-11-02.canDo: I can describe how a city or neighbourhood has changed.

b1-11-03.title: Communicative Challenge: City Problems
b1-11-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos talk about the problems of your area in Budapest: too many cars, so more pollution.
b1-11-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the problem is and what it causes.
cues: Say what the problem is
Say what it causes
b1-11-03.target: Hay demasiados carros, por eso hay más contaminación y mucho ruido.
b1-11-03.english: There are too many cars, so there is more pollution and a lot of noise.
b1-11-03.canDo: I can describe common urban problems.

b1-11-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Should the Council Do?
b1-11-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what the city council should do for pedestrians in your area.
b1-11-04.prompt: Recommend what the council should do and why.
cues: Recommend an action
Say who it helps
b1-11-04.target: Recomiendo que el ayuntamiento mejore las aceras para que los peatones puedan caminar con seguridad.
b1-11-04.english: I recommend that the city council improve the pavements so that pedestrians can walk safely.
b1-11-04.canDo: I can make recommendations for improving a city.

b1-11-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Coketown and Our Meeting
b1-11-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have read about Coketown, the smoky factory town in Dickens's novel, and you take part in a neighbourhood meeting with Carlos. Tell him what the town was like and what you propose.
b1-11-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Coketown was like and make a proposal.
cues: Say what Coketown was like
Make a proposal
b1-11-05.target: Coketown era una ciudad con mucho humo y calles todas iguales. Propongo que haya más parques para las personas.
b1-11-05.english: Coketown was a town with a lot of smoke and streets that were all the same. I propose that there be more parks for people.
b1-11-05.canDo: I can participate in a community discussion.

b1-11-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Better Area
b1-11-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you would do to improve your area in Budapest.
b1-11-consolidation.prompt: Say what is necessary and make a proposal.
cues: Say what the council needs to do
Make a proposal
b1-11-consolidation.target: Es necesario que el ayuntamiento reduzca el tráfico, por eso propongo que construyamos un parque.
b1-11-consolidation.english: It is necessary for the council to reduce traffic, so I propose that we build a park.
b1-11-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate city and neighbourhood language.

b1-12-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Weekday Meals
b1-12-01.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks about your eating habits. You normally have breakfast early, but at weekends you eat later because you have more time.
b1-12-01.prompt: Tell Carlos when you normally have breakfast and what changes at weekends.
cues: Say what you normally do
Say what changes at weekends
Say why
b1-12-01.target: Normalmente desayuno temprano, aunque los fines de semana como más tarde porque tengo más tiempo.
b1-12-01.english: I normally have breakfast early, although at weekends I eat later because I have more time.
b1-12-01.canDo: I can describe eating habits and frequency.

b1-12-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Grandmother's Recipe
b1-12-02.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks about your family. When you were a child, you visited your grandmother in Madrid every summer, and she prepared a traditional recipe.
b1-12-02.prompt: Tell Meg what your grandmother used to prepare every summer when you were a child.
cues: Say when you were a child
Say what your grandmother prepared
Say how often
b1-12-02.target: Cuando era niño, mi abuela preparaba una receta tradicional cada verano.
b1-12-02.english: When I was a child, my grandmother used to prepare a traditional recipe every summer.
b1-12-02.canDo: I can describe food traditions in the past.

b1-12-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Eat Better
b1-12-03.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos says he wants to eat better. You think he should limit sugar and choose nutritious food.
b1-12-03.prompt: Advise Carlos about sugar and nutritious food.
cues: Recommend something about sugar
Recommend something about food
Give a reason
b1-12-03.target: Te recomiendo que moderes el azúcar y que elijas alimentos nutritivos porque son mejores para tu salud.
b1-12-03.english: I recommend that you limit sugar and choose nutritious foods because they are better for your health.
b1-12-03.canDo: I can give advice about food and health.

b1-12-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Home or Out
b1-12-04.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks whether it is better to cook at home or eat out. Cooking at home is usually cheaper, but it takes more time.
b1-12-04.prompt: Compare cooking at home with eating out for Meg.
cues: Say which is cheaper
Add a contrast about time
b1-12-04.target: Cocinar en casa suele ser más barato que comer fuera, aunque requiere más tiempo.
b1-12-04.english: Cooking at home is usually cheaper than eating out, although it takes more time.
b1-12-04.canDo: I can compare how people eat and live.

b1-12-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Doña Rosa's Picantería
b1-12-05.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks what happens in the story of doña Rosa that you read in Spanish. A viceroy asked her to open a stall near the palace, but she preferred to stay in the neighbourhood.
b1-12-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the viceroy asked doña Rosa and what she preferred.
cues: Say what the viceroy recommended
Say what doña Rosa preferred
Say why
b1-12-05.target: El virrey le recomendó abrir un puesto cerca del palacio, pero doña Rosa prefirió quedarse en el barrio.
b1-12-05.english: The viceroy recommended that she open a stall near the palace, but doña Rosa preferred to stay in the neighbourhood.
b1-12-05.canDo: I can describe how eating and lifestyle habits change.

b1-12-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Sunday Lunch
b1-12-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks about your Sunday meals. Your family used to eat together on Sundays, but over time you changed the routine.
b1-12-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what your family used to do and what changed.
cues: Say what your family used to do
Say what changed over time
b1-12-consolidation.target: Antes mi familia comía junta los domingos, pero con el tiempo cambiamos la rutina.
b1-12-consolidation.english: My family used to eat together on Sundays, but over time we changed the routine.
b1-12-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate food and lifestyle vocabulary.

b1-13-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Official Source
b1-13-01.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks what the news says about a strange incident. According to the official source, it happened during the night.
b1-13-01.prompt: Tell Meg what the official source says about when the incident happened.
cues: Name the source
Say when the incident happened
b1-13-01.target: Según la fuente oficial, el suceso ocurrió durante la noche.
b1-13-01.english: According to the official source, the incident happened during the night.
b1-13-01.canDo: I can report information and identify its source.

b1-13-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Witness Said
b1-13-02.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks what the witness said on the news. She said that she had seen a light from her window.
b1-13-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what the witness said.
cues: Say who spoke
Say what she had seen
Say where she had seen it
b1-13-02.target: La testigo dijo que había visto una luz desde su ventana.
b1-13-02.english: The witness said that she had seen a light from her window.
b1-13-02.canDo: I can report what another person said.

b1-13-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Is It Reliable?
b1-13-03.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks whether you trust a news source. You doubt that it is completely reliable, but it may have more information.
b1-13-03.prompt: Tell Meg what you think about the source.
cues: Say you doubt the source is reliable
Say it is possible it has more information
b1-13-03.target: No creo que la fuente sea fiable, pero es posible que tenga más información.
b1-13-03.english: I do not think the source is reliable, but it is possible that it has more information.
b1-13-03.canDo: I can separate facts from opinions and doubt.

b1-13-04.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Story Developed
b1-13-04.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks how the news story developed. First the information from witnesses arrived, later a recording appeared, and finally the investigators explained what had happened.
b1-13-04.prompt: Tell Carlos the three stages of the story in order.
cues: Say what happened first
Say what happened later
Say how it ended
b1-13-04.target: Primero llegó la información de los testigos, posteriormente apareció una grabación y finalmente los investigadores explicaron qué había sucedido.
b1-13-04.english: First the information from the witnesses arrived, later a recording appeared, and finally the investigators explained what had happened.
b1-13-04.canDo: I can follow and explain the development of a news story.

b1-13-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Statue in the Bay
b1-13-05.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks about the chronicle on the Statue of Liberty that you read in Spanish. Thousands of people met in the bay, and many immigrants cried.
cues: Say what thousands of people did
Say how many immigrants reacted and why
b1-13-05.target: Muchas personas se reunieron en la bahía para ver la estatua, y muchos inmigrantes lloraron porque para ellos era un comienzo nuevo.
b1-13-05.english: Thousands of people met in the bay to see the statue, and many immigrants cried because for them it represented a new beginning.
b1-13-05.canDo: I can summarise a news report clearly.

b1-13-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Witnesses and Doubt
b1-13-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks what the news said about the strange light and what you think. According to the witnesses a light appeared, but you do not think the information is reliable yet.
b1-13-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the witnesses said and what you think.
cues: Report what the witnesses said
Say what you think about the information
b1-13-consolidation.target: Según los testigos, apareció una luz, pero no creo que la información sea fiable todavía.
b1-13-consolidation.english: According to the witnesses, a light appeared, but I do not think the information is reliable yet.
b1-13-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate media and information vocabulary.

b1-14-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Staying in Touch
b1-14-01.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks how you stay in touch with your sisters. You normally send messages during the day.
b1-14-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how you normally stay in touch with Lauren and Kaylee.
cues: Say how you normally communicate
Say when
b1-14-01.target: Normalmente envío mensajes durante el día a mis hermanas.
b1-14-01.english: I normally send messages to my sisters during the day.
b1-14-01.canDo: I can describe current communication habits.

b1-14-02.title: Communicative Challenge: My New Phone
b1-14-02.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks what you have done with your phone. You have updated it recently, and now you use it differently.
b1-14-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you have done with your phone.
cues: Say what you have done
Say when
b1-14-02.english: I have updated my device recently.
b1-14-02.canDo: I can describe changes brought by technology.

b1-14-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Call or Message
b1-14-03.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks whether a video call is better than a message. A video call is more immediate than an email, although an email lets you think.
b1-14-03.prompt: Compare a video call with an email for Carlos.
cues: Say which is more immediate
Add a contrast
b1-14-03.target: La videollamada es más inmediata que el correo electrónico, aunque el correo me permite pensar.
b1-14-03.english: A video call is more immediate than email, although email lets me think.

b1-14-04.title: Communicative Challenge: No Internet
b1-14-04.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks what you would do without internet. You would depend more on the phone.
b1-14-04.prompt: Tell Meg what would happen if you did not have internet.
cues: Say the imaginary situation
Say the consequence
b1-14-04.target: Si no tuviéramos internet, dependeríamos más del teléfono.
b1-14-04.english: If we did not have internet, we would depend more on the telephone.
b1-14-04.canDo: I can discuss life without technology.

b1-14-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Monastery Letter
b1-14-05.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks about the letter from a monastery that you read in Spanish. The writer walks in the cloister in the morning and talks with the villagers in the afternoon.
b1-14-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the writer does in the morning and in the afternoon.
cues: Say what he does in the morning
Say what he does in the afternoon
b1-14-05.target: Por la mañana el hombre sale a caminar por el claustro, y por la tarde habla con los campesinos del pueblo.
b1-14-05.english: In the morning the writer goes for a walk in the cloister, and in the afternoon he talks with the villagers.
b1-14-05.canDo: I can discuss the effects of digital life.

b1-14-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Pros and Cons
b1-14-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks what you think of screens. You see an advantage and a disadvantage.
b1-14-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos one advantage and one disadvantage of technology.
cues: Say an advantage
Say a disadvantage with a contrast
b1-14-consolidation.target: Por una parte, la tecnología facilita la comunicación; por otra parte, puede afectar a la privacidad.
b1-14-consolidation.english: On the one hand, technology makes communication easier; on the other hand, it can affect privacy.
b1-14-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate technology and communication vocabulary.

b1-15-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Film or Novel?
b1-15-01.scenario: You are Meg. It is Saturday evening in Budapest and you and Carlos are choosing what to do. He asks whether you would rather watch a film or read a novel.
b1-15-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which you prefer and give a reason.
cues: Say which you prefer, films or novels
Give a reason for your choice
b1-15-01.target: Prefiero las novelas porque puedo imaginar mejor a los personajes.
b1-15-01.english: I prefer novels because I can imagine the characters better.
b1-15-01.canDo: I can express preferences about films, books and music.

b1-15-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Did You Think?
b1-15-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg saw a film in Budapest on Friday evening. Meg asks what you thought of it.
b1-15-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you think of the plot and the characters.
cues: Give your view of the plot
Give your view of the characters
b1-15-02.target: El argumento resulta convincente y los personajes están bien desarrollados.
b1-15-02.english: The plot is convincing and the characters are well developed.
b1-15-02.canDo: I can evaluate cultural works using specific criteria.

b1-15-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Film to Watch
b1-15-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos is looking for something to watch this weekend in Budapest. You saw a film last week and loved it.
b1-15-03.prompt: Recommend the film to Carlos and say why.
cues: Recommend that he watches the film
Give a reason about the plot
b1-15-03.target: Te recomiendo que veas esta película porque el argumento resulta convincente.
b1-15-03.english: I recommend that you watch this film because the plot is convincing.
b1-15-03.canDo: I can recommend cultural works to another person.

b1-15-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Film and Novel
b1-15-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg is reading a novel that was made into a film, and she asks how the two compare.
b1-15-04.prompt: Compare the film with the novel for Meg.
cues: Say which is longer
Add a fact about the novel
b1-15-04.target: La película es más breve que la novela, que tiene un protagonista muy interesante.
b1-15-04.english: The film is shorter than the novel, which has a very interesting protagonist.
b1-15-04.canDo: I can compare films, books and other works.

b1-15-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Night at the Theatre
b1-15-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have just read a short story about a night at the theatre and you tell Carlos what the narrator thinks of the actor and the actress.
b1-15-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the narrator thinks of the actor and of the actress.
cues: Say what the narrator thinks of the actor
Say why the narrator loves the actress
b1-15-05.target: Piensa que el actor es bueno, pero le encanta la actriz porque tiene una voz muy buena.
b1-15-05.english: The narrator thinks the actor is good, but loves the actress because she has a very good voice.
b1-15-05.canDo: I can write a connected cultural review.

b1-15-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Should I Read It?
b1-15-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you about a novel you have just read in Budapest and whether she should read it too.
b1-15-consolidation.prompt: Give Meg your evaluation and a recommendation.
cues: Say what you think of the novel
Recommend that she reads it
b1-15-consolidation.target: Me parece una novela original y te recomiendo que la leas.
b1-15-consolidation.english: The novel seems original to me and I recommend that you read it.
b1-15-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate culture and entertainment vocabulary.

b1-16-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Peaceful Place
b1-16-01.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks you what the place where you grew up is like. It was a village next to a lake, with a forest nearby.
b1-16-01.prompt: Describe your village to Meg using a relative clause.
cues: Say what kind of place it is
Add a fact about the forest or the lake
b1-16-01.target: Es un pueblo donde hay un bosque muy tranquilo cerca del lago.
b1-16-01.english: It is a village where there is a very peaceful forest near the lake.
b1-16-01.canDo: I can describe natural environments and environmental features.

b1-16-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Fewer Trees
b1-16-02.scenario: You are Meg. You walk with Carlos through a park near your flat in Budapest, and he asks if it has changed since you arrived.
b1-16-02.prompt: Tell Carlos how the park has changed.
cues: Say what there used to be
Say what there is now
b1-16-02.target: Ha cambiado mucho: antes había más árboles, pero ahora hay menos.
b1-16-02.english: It has changed a lot: there used to be more trees, but now there are fewer.
b1-16-02.canDo: I can describe environmental change from past to present.

b1-16-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Saving Water at the Office
b1-16-03.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest, a colleague asks what the company should do about water.
b1-16-03.prompt: Say what is necessary and who has to act.
cues: Say what is necessary
Say who has to act
b1-16-03.target: Es necesario que reduzcamos el consumo de agua en la oficina.
b1-16-03.english: It is necessary that we reduce water consumption in the office.
b1-16-03.canDo: I can discuss what environmental action is necessary.

b1-16-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Is There Less Water?
b1-16-04.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate at your university in Budapest asks why the river is so low this year.
b1-16-04.prompt: Give the cause and the consequence.
cues: Give the cause
Say what follows from it
b1-16-04.target: Hay menos agua porque ha habido una sequía; por eso, debemos actuar.
b1-16-04.english: There is less water because there has been a drought; therefore, we must act.
b1-16-04.canDo: I can explain environmental causes and consequences.

b1-16-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Youngest Cub
b1-16-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have just read a story about coati cubs and two children, and you tell Carlos what the youngest cub did.
b1-16-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the youngest cub did and why.
cues: Say where the cub went
Say why he went
b1-16-05.target: El cachorro bajó a la granja porque tenía hambre y quería huevos.
b1-16-05.english: The cub went down to the farm because he was hungry and wanted eggs.
b1-16-05.canDo: I can describe an environmental problem and propose a solution.

b1-16-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Problem and Solution
b1-16-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you what the biggest environmental problem is and what to do about it.
b1-16-consolidation.prompt: Name the problem, the cause and a solution.
cues: Name the problem and its cause
Propose a solution
b1-16-consolidation.target: La contaminación aumenta porque producimos demasiados residuos; por eso, es necesario que reciclemos más.
b1-16-consolidation.english: Pollution increases because we produce too much waste; therefore, it is necessary that we recycle more.

b1-17-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Not the Same for Everyone
b1-17-01.scenario: You are Carlos. After a talk at your office in Budapest, Meg asks you why some children do better at school than others.
b1-17-01.prompt: Compare the families and say what is not equal.
cues: Compare the resources of two families
Mention access to education
b1-17-01.target: Algunas familias tienen más recursos que otras y el acceso a la educación no es igual para todos.
b1-17-01.english: Some families have more resources than others and access to education is not equal for everyone.
b1-17-01.canDo: I can compare different people's opportunities and circumstances.

b1-17-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Poverty?
b1-17-02.scenario: You are Meg. A classmate at your university in Budapest asks you why poverty exists.
b1-17-02.prompt: Give one cause and say that there are several.
cues: Give one cause
Say that the situation is complex
b1-17-02.target: La pobreza puede aumentar debido al desempleo, porque la situación es compleja y existen varias causas.
b1-17-02.english: Poverty can increase due to unemployment, because the situation is complex and there are several causes.
b1-17-02.canDo: I can explain possible causes of inequality and poverty.

b1-17-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Should We Do?
b1-17-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Your colleagues at the office in Budapest ask what should be done to help families with fewer resources.
cues: Say what is necessary
Say what is important
b1-17-03.target: Es necesario que el Gobierno apoye a las familias y es importante que mejoremos el acceso a la educación.
b1-17-03.english: It is necessary that the government support families and it is important that we improve access to education.
b1-17-03.canDo: I can discuss what should be done about inequality.

b1-17-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Polite No
b1-17-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says that education alone solves inequality. You do not fully agree.
b1-17-04.prompt: Disagree politely and give a reason.
cues: Say you understand his argument
Say you disagree and give a reason
b1-17-04.target: Entiendo el argumento, pero no estoy de acuerdo porque creo que falta otra medida.
b1-17-04.english: I understand the argument, but I do not agree because I think another measure is missing.
b1-17-04.canDo: I can express agreement and disagreement respectfully.

b1-17-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Fortunata and Jacinta
b1-17-05.scenario: You are Meg. You have read a story about two women in Madrid and you tell Carlos about it.
b1-17-05.prompt: Tell Carlos how the two women differ and what they share.
cues: Compare the two women
Say who they both love
b1-17-05.target: Fortunata tiene menos dinero que Jacinta, pero las dos quieren a Juanito. Jacinta no puede tener hijos.
b1-17-05.english: Fortunata has less money than Jacinta, but both love Juanito. Jacinta cannot have children.
b1-17-05.canDo: I can discuss a social problem in a sustained way.

b1-17-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Society and Responsibility
b1-17-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you at home in Budapest what you think about inequality and what to do.
b1-17-consolidation.prompt: Give a cause, an opinion and a recommendation.
cues: Give one cause
Give your opinion and a recommendation
b1-17-consolidation.target: La desigualdad tiene varias causas; creo que es necesario que mejoremos el acceso a la educación.
b1-17-consolidation.english: Inequality has several causes; I think it is necessary that we improve access to education.

b1-18-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A New Law
b1-18-01.scenario: You are Meg. In your class at the university in Budapest you have read a news story about a new law. Carlos phones from his office and asks what happened to it. Parliament approved it.
b1-18-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the law and who did it.
cues: Say what happened to the law
Say who approved it
b1-18-01.target: La ley fue aprobada por el Parlamento.
b1-18-01.english: The law was approved by Parliament.
b1-18-01.canDo: I can describe how public processes and government actions work.

b1-18-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Public Transport
b1-18-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Over dinner in your flat in Budapest, Meg asks what you think the city government should do. You think public transport needs work.
b1-18-02.prompt: Tell Meg what the government should improve, using an expression of advisability.
cues: Say it is advisable that something happens
Say what the government should improve
b1-18-02.target: Conviene que el Gobierno mejore el transporte público.
b1-18-02.english: It is advisable that the government improve public transport.
b1-18-02.canDo: I can discuss what governments should do.

b1-18-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Costly Proposal
b1-18-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos shows you a news article about a proposal for a new service in Budapest. You like the proposal, but the service would be very expensive.
b1-18-03.prompt: Give Carlos your opinion of the proposal and say what worries you.
cues: Give your opinion of the proposal
Say what worries you about the price
b1-18-03.target: Creo que la propuesta es positiva. Me parece preocupante que el servicio sea tan caro.
b1-18-03.english: I think the proposal is positive. It seems worrying to me that the service is so expensive.
b1-18-03.canDo: I can express and evaluate political opinions.

b1-18-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Careful Yes
b1-18-04.scenario: You are Carlos. At a neighbourhood debate in Budapest, Meg, who is studying there, asks whether you agree with a proposal. You do agree, but you think it may be hard to carry out.
b1-18-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you agree, and then qualify your view.
cues: Say that you agree with the proposal
Add a difficulty with a contrast
b1-18-04.target: Estoy de acuerdo con la propuesta. Sin embargo, puede ser difícil aplicarla.
b1-18-04.english: I agree with the proposal. However, it may be difficult to implement it.
b1-18-04.canDo: I can participate in a public debate.

b1-18-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Facundo and the Caudillos
b1-18-05.scenario: You are Meg. For a class in Budapest you read a retelling of Sarmiento's book about Facundo Quiroga. Carlos asks what the text says.
b1-18-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the text says about the caudillo and what changed with time.
cues: Say what happened to those who did not obey
Say what Sarmiento defended
b1-18-05.target: Facundo era un caudillo. Se castigaba al que no obedecía. Sarmiento defendía las leyes y las elecciones.
b1-18-05.english: Facundo was a caudillo. Whoever did not obey was punished. Sarmiento defended laws and elections.
b1-18-05.canDo: I can contribute to a public meeting.

b1-18-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Neighbourhood Meeting
b1-18-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At a neighbourhood meeting in Budapest, Meg asks what you think of a new plan. You like it, but you want the people to look at other options too.
b1-18-consolidation.prompt: Give your opinion, add a contrast and recommend an action.
cues: Give your opinion of the plan
Add a contrast
Recommend studying other options
b1-18-consolidation.target: Creo que la propuesta es buena; sin embargo, es necesario que estudiemos otras opciones.
b1-18-consolidation.english: I think the proposal is good; however, it is necessary that we study other options.
b1-18-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate political and public-life vocabulary.

b1-19-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Too Much on Food
b1-19-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos, who works in an office in Budapest, asks you how your money is going this month. You have spent much more on food than last month.
b1-19-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you spend too much on and compare it with last month.
cues: Say what you spend too much on
Compare this month with last month
b1-19-01.target: Este mes gasto demasiado en comida. Tengo más gastos que el mes pasado.
b1-19-01.english: This month I spend too much on food. I have more expenses than last month.
b1-19-01.canDo: I can discuss personal money management.

b1-19-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Rising Prices
b1-19-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg, a student in Budapest, asks you whether things are more expensive now. You think prices have gone up this year.
b1-19-02.prompt: Tell Meg what has happened to prices this year and compare them with before.
cues: Say what has happened to prices
Compare with before
b1-19-02.target: Los precios han subido este año. Algunos productos son más caros que antes.
b1-19-02.english: Prices have risen this year. Some products are more expensive than before.
b1-19-02.canDo: I can describe changes in prices.

b1-19-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Is It So Expensive?
b1-19-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you why a product you want to buy is so expensive. There is little supply of it.
b1-19-03.prompt: Explain to Carlos why the price is high and what happens next.
cues: Give the cause
Give the consequence
b1-19-03.target: Hay poca oferta; por eso, el precio aumenta.
b1-19-03.english: There is little supply; therefore, the price increases.
b1-19-03.canDo: I can explain why prices and costs change.

b1-19-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Higher Salary
b1-19-04.scenario: You are Carlos. In your flat in Budapest, Meg asks what you would do with a higher salary at your office.
b1-19-04.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do if you had a higher salary.
cues: Say what you would do with the money
Use an imagined situation
b1-19-04.target: Si tuviera un salario mayor, ahorraría más.
b1-19-04.english: If I had a higher salary, I would save more.
b1-19-04.canDo: I can discuss hypothetical financial decisions.

b1-19-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Friar and the Scorpion
b1-19-05.scenario: You are Carlos. For a talk, you read a retelling of a Peruvian tradition about Fray Gómez, inspired by Ricardo Palma. Meg, who studies in Budapest, asks you what the story is about.
b1-19-05.prompt: Tell Meg what the friar gave the woman and what happened with the debt.
cues: Say what the friar gave the woman
Say what the scorpion was in the city
Say what happened with the debt
b1-19-05.target: Fray Gómez le dio un alacrán en un papel. El alacrán era una joya y la mujer pagó la deuda.
b1-19-05.english: Fray Gómez gave her a scorpion in a paper. The scorpion was a jewel and the woman paid the debt.
b1-19-05.canDo: I can discuss economic trends and opinions.

b1-19-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Prices and Plans
b1-19-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about the economy. You see that prices are rising, and you would save more if you could.
b1-19-consolidation.prompt: Describe a trend, say what you would do and give a reason.
cues: Describe a trend in prices
Say what you would do
Give a reason
b1-19-consolidation.target: Se observa que los precios están aumentando. Si pudiera, ahorraría más.
b1-19-consolidation.english: It can be seen that prices are rising. If I could, I would save more.
b1-19-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate money and economic vocabulary.

b1-20-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Broken Lift
b1-20-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos phones from his office in Budapest. You tell him about the building you live in, where a breakdown has stopped the lift. Many neighbours depend on it.
b1-20-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which building has the breakdown and what the breakdown affects.
cues: Say which building has the breakdown
Say what the breakdown affects
b1-20-01.target: Hay una avería en el edificio en el que vivimos. Afecta a un servicio del que dependen muchos vecinos.
b1-20-01.english: There is a breakdown in the building we live in. It affects a service on which many neighbours depend.
b1-20-01.canDo: I can describe problems precisely and explain what they affect.

b1-20-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why It Got Worse
b1-20-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you why the breakdown in your office building got worse. Nobody acted in time.
b1-20-02.prompt: Tell Meg what caused the problem to get worse and what was needed afterwards.
cues: Give the cause
Say what was needed afterwards
b1-20-02.target: El problema se agravó porque no se actuó a tiempo. Por eso fue necesario buscar otra solución.
b1-20-02.english: The problem got worse because action was not taken in time. So it was necessary to look for another solution.
b1-20-02.canDo: I can explain why problems happen and what follows.

b1-20-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Act Now
b1-20-03.scenario: You are Meg. At a neighbours' meeting in Budapest, Carlos asks what you think should be done about the breakdowns.
b1-20-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what is necessary and why.
cues: Say what is necessary
Say why we should act
b1-20-03.target: Es necesario que actuemos a tiempo. Hace falta que prevengamos nuevas averías.
b1-20-03.english: It is necessary that we act in time. We need to prevent new breakdowns.
b1-20-03.canDo: I can discuss what needs to be done about a problem.

b1-20-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Second Option
b1-20-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you would do at the office if the first solution to the problem did not work.
b1-20-04.prompt: Tell Meg what you would do if the first solution did not work.
cues: Say what you would look for
Say under what condition
b1-20-04.target: Buscaría una alternativa si la primera solución no funcionara.
b1-20-04.english: I would look for an alternative if the first solution did not work.

b1-20-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Paulino and the River
b1-20-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a retelling of a story by Horacio Quiroga for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what happens in it.
b1-20-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what happens to Paulino and where he wants to go.
cues: Say what bites Paulino
Say where he wants to go
Say how the story ends
b1-20-05.target: Una serpiente muerde a Paulino. Él sube a su canoa para llegar a Tacurú-Pucú, pero no llega.
b1-20-05.english: A snake bites Paulino. He gets into his canoe to reach Tacurú-Pucú, but he does not arrive.
b1-20-05.canDo: I can discuss a problem from diagnosis to solution.

b1-20-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Choosing a Solution
b1-20-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest you have to explain a problem to Meg, who is visiting. The problem got worse because nobody acted, and you want to propose a plan.
b1-20-consolidation.prompt: Say what happened, why, and what is necessary now.
cues: Say what happened to the problem
Give the cause
Say what is necessary now
b1-20-consolidation.target: El problema se agravó porque no se actuó a tiempo. Es necesario que abordemos su causa.
b1-20-consolidation.english: The problem got worse because action was not taken in time. It is necessary that we address its cause.

b1-21-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Giving Your Opinion
b1-21-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about the city's proposal to close the centre of Budapest to cars on Sundays. You like it, and you have a reason.
b1-21-01.prompt: Tell Carlos your opinion about the proposal and give a reason.
cues: Say what you think of the proposal
Give a reason
b1-21-01.target: Me parece que la propuesta es razonable porque ayuda a muchas personas.
b1-21-01.english: It seems to me that the proposal is reasonable because it helps many people.
b1-21-01.canDo: I can express an opinion and give a reason.

b1-21-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Agreeing, But...
b1-21-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg likes the Sunday proposal for the centre of Budapest. You agree with it, but you think it needs some changes.
b1-21-02.prompt: Tell Meg that you agree, but that the proposal needs changes.
cues: Say you agree
Say what you think it needs
b1-21-02.target: Estoy de acuerdo con la propuesta, pero creo que necesita algunos cambios.
b1-21-02.english: I agree with the proposal, but I think it needs some changes.
b1-21-02.canDo: I can agree partly and disagree respectfully.

b1-21-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What a Good Debate Needs
b1-21-03.scenario: You are Meg. Your class at the university in Budapest is preparing a debate, and Carlos asks what is important for it to go well.
b1-21-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what is important and what is necessary for a good debate.
cues: Say what is important
Say what is necessary
b1-21-03.target: Es importante que escuchemos opiniones diferentes. Es necesario que consideremos la evidencia.
b1-21-03.english: It is important that we listen to different opinions. It is necessary that we consider the evidence.
b1-21-03.canDo: I can evaluate ideas and discuss what is necessary.

b1-21-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Backing Up a View
b1-21-04.scenario: You are Carlos. At your office in Budapest your team compares two plans. Meg asks which one you support and why.
b1-21-04.prompt: Tell Meg which plan you support, why, and how the other plan differs.
cues: Say which plan you support and why
Say how the other plan is different
b1-21-04.target: Apoyo la primera propuesta porque es más sencilla. En cambio, la segunda tendría más costes.
b1-21-04.english: I support the first proposal because it is simpler. By contrast, the second would have more costs.
b1-21-04.canDo: I can support opinions with reasons and evidence.

b1-21-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Short Essay on Opinions
b1-21-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a short essay in the style of the Paliques by Clarín for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what the writer says.
b1-21-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what many people do and what the writer asks of them.
cues: Say what many people do
Say what the writer asks
b1-21-05.target: Muchas personas dan su opinión sin pensarlo antes. La persona que escribe pide que reconozcan lo que saben y lo que no saben.
b1-21-05.english: Many people give their opinion without thinking first. The writer asks them to recognise what they know and what they do not know.
b1-21-05.canDo: I can take part in a sustained debate.

b1-21-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Condition and a Conclusion
b1-21-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks whether you support the Sunday proposal after all. You see some limitations, but you have a condition.
b1-21-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg your conclusion about the proposal and your condition.
cues: Admit a limitation
Give your conclusion and a condition
b1-21-consolidation.target: Aunque tiene algunas limitaciones, la propuesta es útil. Apoyo la medida siempre que ayude a todos.
b1-21-consolidation.english: Although it has some limitations, the proposal is useful. I support the measure as long as it helps everyone.
b1-21-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate opinion and debate vocabulary.

b1-22-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Is She?
b1-22-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks where your sister Lauren is. She is not answering her phone. You guess she is at home, but you are not sure.
b1-22-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where you think Lauren is and that you are not sure.
cues: Say where you think she is
Say you are not sure
b1-22-01.target: Estará en casa, pero no estoy segura.
b1-22-01.english: She is probably at home, but I am not sure.
b1-22-01.canDo: I can use the future to make predictions and guesses.

b1-22-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Perhaps on Friday
b1-22-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether your brother Andreas will visit you in Budapest next week. You are not sure, but perhaps he will arrive on Friday.
b1-22-02.prompt: Tell Meg that perhaps Andreas will arrive on Friday and that you are not sure.
cues: Say when he may arrive
Say you are not sure
b1-22-02.target: Quizá llegue el viernes, pero no estoy seguro.
b1-22-02.english: Perhaps he will arrive on Friday, but I am not sure.
b1-22-02.canDo: I can express different degrees of probability.

b1-22-03.title: Communicative Challenge: With More Time
b1-22-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you would do if you had more free time in Budapest. You would visit his grandmother in Madrid.
b1-22-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would do if you had more time.
cues: Say the condition
Say what you would do
b1-22-03.target: Si tuviera más tiempo, visitaría a tu abuela en Madrid.
b1-22-03.english: If I had more time, I would visit your grandmother in Madrid.
b1-22-03.canDo: I can describe hypothetical situations and their consequences.

b1-22-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Different Life
b1-22-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what life would be like if you both lived in Madrid, where your grandmother lives.
b1-22-04.prompt: Tell Meg what life might be like if you lived in Madrid.
cues: Imagine the situation
Say how sure you are
b1-22-04.target: Si viviéramos en Madrid, quizá tendríamos una vida diferente.
b1-22-04.english: If we lived in Madrid, perhaps we would have a different life.
b1-22-04.canDo: I can imagine alternative future scenarios.

b1-22-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Blue Bird
b1-22-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a retelling of a story by Rubén Darío for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what happens in it.
b1-22-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the poet Garcín says and what he does when his father writes to him.
cues: Say what Garcín says about a bird
Say what he does with his father's letter
b1-22-05.target: Un poeta llamado Garcín dice que tiene un pájaro azul en la cabeza. Su padre le escribe una carta, pero Garcín no acepta el trabajo.
b1-22-05.english: A poet called Garcín says he has a blue bird in his head. His father writes him a letter, but Garcín does not accept the job.
b1-22-05.canDo: I can make predictions using evidence and trends.

b1-22-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Prices Next Year
b1-22-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you what will happen to prices in Budapest next year. The trend says they will rise, but you are not sure.
b1-22-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what the trend says and that things may change.
cues: Say what the trend says
Say it may change
b1-22-consolidation.target: Según la tendencia actual, los precios subirán, aunque es posible que cambie la situación.
b1-22-consolidation.english: According to the current trend, prices will rise, although the situation may change.

b1-23-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Which Café?
b1-23-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks which of two cafés in Budapest you would recommend for the next language exchange. The first one is cheaper than the second.
b1-23-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which café you would choose and why.
cues: Say which café you would choose
Compare the prices
b1-23-01.target: Creo que sería mejor elegir el primer café porque es más barato.
b1-23-01.english: I think it would be better to choose the first café because it is cheaper.
b1-23-01.canDo: I can compare options and make a recommendation.

b1-23-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Sides
b1-23-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you about the two cafés. The first one is cheap, but it is less comfortable.
b1-23-02.prompt: Tell Meg one advantage and one disadvantage of the first café.
cues: Say one advantage
Say one disadvantage
b1-23-02.target: Por un lado, el primero es barato; por otro lado, es menos cómodo.
b1-23-02.english: On the one hand, the first one is cheap; on the other hand, it is less comfortable.
b1-23-02.canDo: I can present advantages and disadvantages.

b1-23-03.title: Communicative Challenge: If We Choose the Second
b1-23-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what will happen if you both choose the second café. It is more expensive, but it is quiet.
b1-23-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the consequences of choosing the second café will be.
cues: Say the condition
Say the two consequences
b1-23-03.target: Si elegimos el segundo, tendremos que pagar más, pero estaremos más tranquilos.
b1-23-03.english: If we choose the second one, we will have to pay more, but we will be calmer.
b1-23-03.canDo: I can describe consequences of choices.

b1-23-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Is It Worth It?
b1-23-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether it is worth paying more for the quiet café. You think it is, and you prefer a calm place.
b1-23-04.prompt: Tell Meg what you think about paying more and what is preferable.
cues: Say whether it is worth it
Say what is preferable
b1-23-04.target: Creo que merece la pena pagar más. Es preferible elegir un lugar más tranquilo.
b1-23-04.english: I think it is worth paying more. It is preferable to choose a quieter place.

b1-23-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Seminarian and the Widow
b1-23-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a retelling of the novel Pepita Jiménez by Juan Valera for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what happens in it.
b1-23-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Luis studies, whom he falls in love with and what he decides.
cues: Say what Luis studies
Say whom he loves and what he decides
b1-23-05.target: Luis de Vargas estudia para ser sacerdote. Se enamora de Pepita, deja el seminario y se casa con ella.
b1-23-05.english: Luis de Vargas studies to be a priest. He falls in love with Pepita, leaves the seminary and marries her.
b1-23-05.canDo: I can reach and justify a decision.

b1-23-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Final Choice
b1-23-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks which café you finally choose and why.
b1-23-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg which café you choose after comparing and give your priority.
cues: Say you compared the two
Say which you choose and why
b1-23-consolidation.target: Después de comparar los dos cafés, creo que es mejor elegir el segundo porque es más tranquilo.
b1-23-consolidation.english: After comparing the two cafés, I think it is better to choose the second because it is quieter.

b1-24-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Using the Machine
b1-24-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg, a student, visits your office in Budapest and wants to use the machine there. You tell her how it works.
b1-24-01.prompt: Tell Meg how to use the machine.
cues: Say what is put into the machine
Say what is pressed to start
b1-24-01.target: Se introduce la tarjeta en la máquina y se pulsa este botón.
b1-24-01.english: The card is put into the machine and this button is pressed.
b1-24-01.canDo: I can explain how something works using impersonal constructions.

b1-24-02.title: Communicative Challenge: First, Next, Finally
b1-24-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos has to start the machine at his office in Budapest for the first time. You know the steps and tell him the order.
b1-24-02.prompt: Tell Carlos the three steps in order.
cues: Say what is done first
Say what is done next
Say what is done at the end
b1-24-02.target: Primero, se enciende la máquina. A continuación, se introduce el material. Finalmente, se comprueba el resultado.
b1-24-02.english: First, the machine is switched on. Next, the material is inserted. Finally, the result is checked.
b1-24-02.canDo: I can sequence the stages of a process clearly.

b1-24-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Made in Spain
b1-24-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Your office in Budapest has a new product from Spain. Meg asks you where it is made and what it is made of.
b1-24-03.prompt: Tell Meg where the product is made and how many parts it has.
cues: Say where it is made
Say how many parts it has
b1-24-03.target: El producto se fabrica en España. Está compuesto de tres partes.
b1-24-03.english: The product is made in Spain. It is made up of three parts.
b1-24-03.canDo: I can describe what objects are made of and how they are produced.

b1-24-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Saving Energy
b1-24-04.scenario: You are Meg. At the language school in Budapest there is a new system. You explain to Carlos how it saves energy.
b1-24-04.prompt: Tell Carlos how the system reduces energy use and what is checked at the end.
cues: Say how energy use is reduced
Say what is checked at the end
b1-24-04.target: Mediante este sistema, se reduce el consumo de energía. Por último, se comprueba que todo funciona correctamente.
b1-24-04.english: By means of this system, energy consumption is reduced. Lastly, it is checked that everything works correctly.
b1-24-04.canDo: I can explain a process using connectors.

b1-24-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Margarita's Shirt
b1-24-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a retelling of «La camisa de Margarita», a tale by Ricardo Palma, for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what happens.
b1-24-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Margarita's father swears and what the shirt is like.
cues: Say what the father swears
Say what the shirt is like
b1-24-05.target: Don Raimundo jura que solo dará a su hija la camisa de novia. La camisa es muy cara.
b1-24-05.english: Don Raimundo swears that he will give his daughter only the wedding shirt. The shirt is very expensive.
b1-24-05.canDo: I can give a complete explanation of a procedure.

b1-24-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: From First to Last
b1-24-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you at your office in Budapest how a process works from the first step to the last.
b1-24-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the steps of the process in order.
cues: Say what is done first
Say what is done next
Say what is checked at the end
b1-24-consolidation.target: Primero se prepara el material. Después se introduce en la máquina y, por último, se comprueba el resultado.
b1-24-consolidation.english: First the material is prepared. Then it is inserted into the machine and, lastly, the result is checked.
b1-24-consolidation.canDo: I can use the process words of this unit.

b1-25-01.title: Communicative Challenge: My Sister Changed
b1-25-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how your sister Lauren is. She has changed a lot: she became a teacher and she was very happy about it.
b1-25-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what your sister became and how she felt.
cues: Say what your sister became
Say how she felt
b1-25-01.target: Mi hermana Lauren se hizo profesora y se puso muy contenta.
b1-25-01.english: My sister Lauren became a teacher and became very happy.
b1-25-01.canDo: I can describe how things change over time.

b1-25-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Then and Now
b1-25-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how your grandmother in Madrid kept in touch with her family before and how people do it today.
b1-25-02.prompt: Tell Meg how communication was before and how it is now.
cues: Say how it was before
Say how it is now
b1-25-02.target: Antes, la comunicación era más lenta. Actualmente, la información circula rápidamente.
b1-25-02.english: Before, communication was slower. Currently, information circulates quickly.
b1-25-02.canDo: I can contrast past and present situations.

b1-25-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Will Change
b1-25-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos, who works in an office in Budapest, asks what you think will happen with work and technology in the future.
b1-25-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think will happen.
cues: Say what will probably exist
Say what will continue
b1-25-03.target: Probablemente habrá nuevas formas de trabajar. La tecnología seguirá cambiando.
b1-25-03.english: There will probably be new ways of working. Technology will continue changing.
b1-25-03.canDo: I can make predictions about future development.

b1-25-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Has to Change
b1-25-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what has to change at your office in Budapest to make work better.
b1-25-04.prompt: Tell Meg what is important and what needs to change.
cues: Say what is important to improve
Say what needs to change
b1-25-04.target: Es importante que mejoremos el sistema. Hace falta que cambien algunas cosas.
b1-25-04.english: It is important that we improve the system. Some things need to change.
b1-25-04.canDo: I can explain what needs to change.

b1-25-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Gabriel and Trafalgar
b1-25-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a retelling of «Trafalgar», a novel by Benito Pérez Galdós, for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what happens.
b1-25-05.prompt: Tell Carlos who Gabriel is and where he goes with the captain.
cues: Say what Gabriel is like as a child
Say where he goes with the captain
b1-25-05.target: Gabriel es un niño huérfano de Cádiz. Va con el capitán don Alonso a la batalla de Trafalgar.
b1-25-05.english: Gabriel is an orphan boy from Cádiz. He goes with Captain don Alonso to the Battle of Trafalgar.
b1-25-05.canDo: I can discuss change and development in an integrated way.

b1-25-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Before and After
b1-25-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks you in Budapest how things have changed and what you think will happen next.
b1-25-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how the situation was before, how it is now and what will probably happen.
cues: Say how it was before
Say how it is now
Say what will probably happen
b1-25-consolidation.target: Antes la situación era diferente, pero actualmente ha cambiado mucho. Probablemente seguirá evolucionando.
b1-25-consolidation.english: The situation was different before, but it has changed a lot now. It will probably continue evolving.
b1-25-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for change and development.

b1-26-01.title: Communicative Challenge: My Plans for Next Year
b1-26-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg, a student, asks what you plan to do next year.
b1-26-01.prompt: Tell Meg what you will do next year and what you want to devote yourself to.
cues: Say what you will look for next year
Say what you want to devote yourself to
b1-26-01.target: El año que viene buscaré un trabajo nuevo. Quiero dedicarme a la investigación.
b1-26-01.english: Next year I will look for a new job. I want to work in research.
b1-26-01.canDo: I can discuss career plans and intentions.

b1-26-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Success?
b1-26-02.scenario: You are Meg. You are a student in Budapest. Carlos asks what success means to you.
b1-26-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what is more important to you, success or money.
cues: Compare success and money
Say it is your opinion
b1-26-02.target: Para mí, el éxito es más importante que el dinero.
b1-26-02.english: For me, success is more important than money.
b1-26-02.canDo: I can evaluate and compare different ideas of success.

b1-26-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Matters Most
b1-26-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg, a student in Budapest, works a lot and has no free time. You tell her what you think is important.
b1-26-03.prompt: Tell Meg what is important and what is better for her.
cues: Say what is important for everyone
Say what is better for her
b1-26-03.target: Es importante que tengamos tiempo para nosotros. Es mejor que busques un equilibrio.
b1-26-03.english: It is important that we have time for ourselves. It is better for you to look for a balance.
b1-26-03.canDo: I can express priorities and opinions about work and life.

b1-26-04.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Had More Time
b1-26-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you would do if you had more free time.
b1-26-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would do if you had more time.
cues: Start with the imagined situation
Say what you would do
b1-26-04.target: Si tuviera más tiempo, viajaría más.
b1-26-04.english: If I had more time, I would travel more.
