b1-26-04.canDo: I can discuss hypothetical choices about work and time.

b1-26-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Marianela and Pablo
b1-26-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a retelling of «Marianela», a novel by Benito Pérez Galdós, for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what happens.
b1-26-05.prompt: Tell Carlos who Pablo is and what the doctor says.
cues: Say what Pablo is like
Say what the doctor says
b1-26-05.target: Pablo es un joven ciego. El doctor lo opera y Pablo puede ver, pero Nela, que lo quería, muere de tristeza.
b1-26-05.english: Pablo is a young blind man. The doctor operates on him and Pablo can see, but Nela, who loved him, dies of grief.
b1-26-05.canDo: I can build a sustained argument about work and success.

b1-26-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Balanced Life
b1-26-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks you what your priority is and what you would change.
b1-26-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg your priority and what you would do with more time.
cues: Say your priority and why
Say what you would do with more time
b1-26-consolidation.target: Para mí, el equilibrio es una prioridad porque necesito tiempo para otras cosas. Si tuviera más tiempo, trabajaría menos.
b1-26-consolidation.english: For me, balance is a priority because I need time for other things. If I had more time, I would work less.
b1-26-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for work and ambition.

b1-27-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Keeping in Touch
b1-27-01.scenario: You are Meg. You are a student in Budapest. Carlos asks how you keep in touch with your sister Lauren.
b1-27-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how you keep in touch with Lauren and what you did yesterday.
cues: Say how you keep in touch with her
Say what you sent her yesterday
b1-27-01.target: Me mantengo en contacto con Lauren por mensaje. Ayer le mandé un mensaje.
b1-27-01.english: I keep in touch with Lauren by message. Yesterday I sent her a message.
b1-27-01.canDo: I can describe how people communicate and keep in touch.

b1-27-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What She Said
b1-27-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks why you came home late, and you tell her about a colleague.
b1-27-02.prompt: Tell Meg what your colleague said and what she asked you.
cues: Say what she said
Say what she asked you
b1-27-02.target: Una compañera me dijo que estaba ocupada y me preguntó si tenía tiempo.
b1-27-02.english: A colleague told me that she was busy and asked me if I had time.
b1-27-02.canDo: I can report basic statements and questions.

b1-27-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Did She Mean?
b1-27-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos shows you a short message from his grandmother in Madrid and says he does not understand it. You think about what she wanted.
b1-27-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what his grandmother wanted to know and what she meant.
cues: Say what she wanted to know
Say what she meant
b1-27-03.target: Tu abuela quería saber si íbamos a Madrid. Quiso decir que quiere vernos.
b1-27-03.english: Your grandmother wanted to know if we were going to Madrid. She meant that she wants to see us.
b1-27-03.canDo: I can explain indirect meaning and intention.

b1-27-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Can You Explain It?
b1-27-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg tells you something about her class and you do not understand. You ask her to explain it, then you understand.
b1-27-04.prompt: Ask Meg to explain and tell her that now you understand.
cues: Ask what she means
Say that now you understand
b1-27-04.target: ¿Puedes explicarlo otra vez? Ahora entiendo lo que querías decir.
b1-27-04.english: Can you explain it again? Now I understand what you meant.
b1-27-04.canDo: I can repair communication problems through clarification.

b1-27-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Don Dimas and the Devil
b1-27-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a simplified retelling of «Don Dimas de la Tijereta», a tale by Ricardo Palma, for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what happens.
b1-27-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Dimas says on the hill and what happens in hell.
cues: Say what Dimas says on the hill
Say what the judges decide
b1-27-05.target: Dimas dice que un diablo puede llevarse su almilla. Los jueces del infierno leen el contrato y deciden que Dimas gana.
b1-27-05.english: Dimas says that a devil can take his waistcoat. The judges in hell read the contract and decide that Dimas wins.
b1-27-05.canDo: I can describe an awkward interaction.

b1-27-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Clearing Up a Message
b1-27-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks what happened with a message from your colleague.
b1-27-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you thought and what your colleague explained.
cues: Say what you thought
Say what she explained
b1-27-consolidation.target: Pensé que estaba triste, pero me explicó que estaba ocupada. Le pregunté qué quería decir y aclaramos el malentendido.
b1-27-consolidation.english: I thought she was sad, but she explained to me that she was busy. I asked her what she meant and we cleared up the misunderstanding.
b1-27-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for communication and misunderstandings.

b1-28-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rules in My Class
b1-28-01.scenario: You are Meg. You are a student in Budapest. Carlos asks what the rules are in your class.
b1-28-01.prompt: Tell Carlos one thing you have to do and one thing that is not allowed.
cues: Say what you have to do
Say what is not allowed
b1-28-01.target: En mi clase hay que llegar a tiempo y no se permite fumar en el edificio.
b1-28-01.english: In my class you have to arrive on time and smoking is not allowed in the building.
b1-28-01.canDo: I can describe rules, obligations and prohibitions.

b1-28-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Allowed at Work
b1-28-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks what is allowed there.
b1-28-02.prompt: Tell Meg what is allowed and what is not allowed in your office.
cues: Say what is allowed
Say what is not allowed
b1-28-02.target: En mi oficina está permitido usar el teléfono, pero no se puede fumar.
b1-28-02.english: In my office using the phone is allowed, but you cannot smoke.
b1-28-02.canDo: I can describe what people are allowed to do.

b1-28-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What Should Happen
b1-28-03.scenario: You are Meg. You live in Budapest. Carlos asks what you think should happen in public life.
b1-28-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what is necessary and what is important for the government.
cues: Say what is necessary for everyone
Say what is important for the government
b1-28-03.target: Es necesario que todos respeten las reglas y es importante que el gobierno escuche a la gente.
b1-28-03.english: It is necessary that everyone respects the rules and it is important that the government listens to the people.
b1-28-03.canDo: I can discuss what should happen in public life.

b1-28-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why We Follow Rules
b1-28-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks why everyone has to follow a rule at work.
b1-28-04.prompt: Tell Meg why we must follow the rule and what it means for everyone.
cues: Give a reason for the rule
Say what it means for everyone
b1-28-04.target: Debemos cumplir la regla porque protege a todos. Por eso es una responsabilidad de todos.
b1-28-04.english: We must follow the rule because it protects everyone. That is why it is everyone's responsibility.
b1-28-04.canDo: I can discuss rights and responsibilities.

b1-28-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Martí and Our America
b1-28-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a simplified retelling of «Nuestra América», an essay by José Martí, for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks what Martí says.
b1-28-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Martí says about the government and about schools.
cues: Say what Martí says about the government
Say what has to be taught in schools
b1-28-05.target: Martí dice que el gobierno tiene que nacer del propio país. También dice que en las escuelas hay que enseñar primero la historia de América.
b1-28-05.english: Martí says that the government has to be born from the country itself. He also says that in schools you have to teach the history of America first.
b1-28-05.canDo: I can defend a position about a difficult rule.

b1-28-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rule at Work
b1-28-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks what you think about a rule at work.
b1-28-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you think of the rule and why we must respect it.
cues: Say what you think and why
Say what our responsibility is
b1-28-consolidation.target: Creo que la regla es necesaria porque protege a todos. Aunque sea incómoda, tenemos la responsabilidad de respetarla.
b1-28-consolidation.english: I think the rule is necessary because it protects everyone. Although it may be inconvenient, we have the responsibility to respect it.
b1-28-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for rules and obligation.

b1-29-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Do I Belong?
b1-29-01.scenario: You are Meg. You are a student in Budapest. Carlos asks where you are from and where you feel at home.
b1-29-01.prompt: Tell Carlos where you are from, where you live and where you belong.
cues: Say where you are from
Say where you live now
Say that you feel part of the city
b1-29-01.target: Soy de Sudáfrica, pero ahora vivo en Budapest. Me siento parte de esta ciudad.
b1-29-01.english: I am from South Africa, but now I live in Budapest. I feel part of this city.
b1-29-01.canDo: I can describe identity, origin and belonging.

b1-29-02.title: Communicative Challenge: My First Days in Budapest
b1-29-02.scenario: You are Meg. You moved to Budapest. Carlos asks how your first days were.
b1-29-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what your first days in Budapest were like.
cues: Say that you moved to Budapest
Say that at first you did not know anyone
Say that you met the neighbours
b1-29-02.target: Me mudé a Budapest y al principio no conocía a nadie. Después conocí a los vecinos.
b1-29-02.english: I moved to Budapest and at first I did not know anyone. Then I met the neighbours.
b1-29-02.canDo: I can describe moving to another country.

b1-29-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting Used to Budapest
b1-29-03.scenario: You are Meg. You have lived in Budapest for a while. Carlos asks how you adapted.
b1-29-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how you adapted and what you got used to.
cues: Say that you adapted little by little
Say what you got used to
Say what you realised one day
b1-29-03.target: Poco a poco me adapté a la ciudad. Me acostumbré a los horarios y un día me di cuenta de que ya conocía el barrio.
b1-29-03.english: Little by little I adapted to the city. I got used to the schedules and one day I realised that I already knew the neighbourhood.
b1-29-03.canDo: I can describe adapting to a new place.

b1-29-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Makes a Home
b1-29-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You live in Budapest. Meg asks what makes a place feel like home.
b1-29-04.prompt: Tell Meg which place is your home and what makes a home.
cues: Say which neighbourhood is your home
Say what makes a home
b1-29-04.target: El barrio donde vivo es mi hogar. Lo que hace un hogar es la gente que conocemos.
b1-29-04.english: The neighbourhood where I live is my home. What makes a home is the people we know.
b1-29-04.canDo: I can explain what makes a place feel like home.

b1-29-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Life of José Martí
b1-29-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a simplified retelling of the life of José Martí for a class in Budapest. Carlos asks about it.
b1-29-05.prompt: Tell Carlos where Martí was from, what happened when he was seventeen and where he lived.
cues: Say where Martí was born
Say what happened when he was seventeen
Say where he lived later
b1-29-05.target: Martí era de La Habana y a los diecisiete años lo enviaron a España. Después vivió en México y en Nueva York, pero siempre se sintió parte de Cuba.
b1-29-05.english: Martí was from Havana and at seventeen they sent him to Spain. Later he lived in Mexico and in New York, but he always felt part of Cuba.
b1-29-05.canDo: I can discuss migration and dual identity.

b1-29-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Origin and Belonging
b1-29-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are Hungarian and you work in an office in Budapest. Meg asks about your identity.
b1-29-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what your origin means for you and what you can keep.
cues: Say that your origin is part of your identity
Say what you can keep and where you belong
b1-29-consolidation.target: Mi origen forma parte de mi identidad. Puedo mantener mis tradiciones y sentirme parte de más de un lugar.
b1-29-consolidation.english: My origin is part of my identity. I can keep my traditions and feel part of more than one place.
b1-29-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for migration and identity.

b1-30-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Accents
b1-30-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks which Spanish accent is easier for you to understand: Daniela's, from Chile, or his grandmother's, from Madrid. You find Daniela's easier.
b1-30-01.prompt: Tell Carlos which accent is easier to understand.
cues: Name the two accents
Say which one is easier to understand
b1-30-01.target: El acento de Daniela es más fácil de entender que el de la abuela de Carlos.
b1-30-01.english: Daniela's accent is easier to understand than Carlos's grandmother's.
b1-30-01.canDo: I can compare different ways of speaking.

b1-30-02.title: Communicative Challenge: My Language, My Identity
b1-30-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether Hungarian is part of who you are, now that you speak Spanish with her every day. You think your language is part of your identity because you speak it with your family.
b1-30-02.prompt: Tell Meg that your language is part of your identity and why.
cues: Give your opinion
Say how language and identity are related
Give a reason
b1-30-02.target: Creo que mi lengua forma parte de mi identidad porque la hablo con mi familia.
b1-30-02.english: I think my language is part of my identity because I speak it with my family.
b1-30-02.canDo: I can explain the relationship between language and identity.

b1-30-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Learning About Other Cultures
b1-30-03.scenario: You are Meg. Your sister Lauren asks on a call whether it is worth learning about Hungarian customs. You think it is good to learn about other cultures and important to respect their traditions.
b1-30-03.prompt: Tell Lauren that it is good to learn about other cultures and important to respect traditions.
cues: Say it is good to learn about other cultures
Say what is important about traditions
b1-30-03.target: Es bueno que conozcamos otras culturas y es importante que respetemos las tradiciones.
b1-30-03.english: It is good that we learn about other cultures and it is important that we respect traditions.
b1-30-03.canDo: I can discuss what culture means.

b1-30-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Family Celebrations
b1-30-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how your family's celebrations compare with her family's. They are different, but both families have something in common.
b1-30-04.prompt: Tell Meg that the two celebrations are different but have something in common.
cues: Say the celebrations are different
Say what they share
b1-30-04.target: Las fiestas de mi familia y las de tu familia son diferentes, pero tienen algo en común.
b1-30-04.english: My family's celebrations and your family's are different, but they have something in common.
b1-30-04.canDo: I can compare cultural similarities and differences.

b1-30-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Grammar for the Americas
b1-30-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what the text about Andrés Bello says. Bello wrote a grammar for the people of Spanish America. He wants the countries to keep a common language, but he accepts their differences.
b1-30-05.prompt: Tell Meg what Bello wrote and what he wants.
cues: Say what Bello wrote and for whom
Say what he wants the countries to keep
Say he accepts their differences
b1-30-05.target: Bello escribió una gramática para la gente de América. Quiere que los países mantengan una lengua común, pero acepta sus diferencias.
b1-30-05.english: Bello wrote a grammar for the Americans. He wants the countries to keep a common language, but he accepts their differences.
b1-30-05.canDo: I can discuss language, culture and identity in a sustained way.

b1-30-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Languages and Cultures
b1-30-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about learning a language and living between two cultures in Budapest. You think differences can be an opportunity, and that listening is as important as speaking.
b1-30-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think about cultural differences and about listening.
cues: Give your opinion on differences
Say what is important
Compare listening with speaking
b1-30-consolidation.target: Creo que las diferencias culturales son una oportunidad para aprender. Es importante que escuchemos, y escuchar es tan importante como hablar.
b1-30-consolidation.english: I think cultural differences are an opportunity to learn. It is important that we listen, and listening is as important as speaking.
b1-30-consolidation.canDo: I can use the vocabulary of language and culture.

b1-31-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Society in Twenty Years
b1-31-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks you over dinner in Budapest what you think society will be like in twenty years. You think it will change a lot and technology will have an important role.
b1-31-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think society will be like.
cues: Say that society will change
Say what role technology will have
b1-31-01.target: La sociedad cambiará mucho y la tecnología tendrá un papel importante.
b1-31-01.english: Society will change a lot and technology will have an important role.
b1-31-01.canDo: I can make predictions about the future of society.

b1-31-02.title: Communicative Challenge: New Professions
b1-31-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether there will be new professions in the future. You think there probably will be, and that work may be different.
b1-31-02.prompt: Tell Meg how likely new professions are and that work may change.
cues: Say there will probably be new professions
Say it is possible that work will be different
b1-31-02.target: Probablemente habrá nuevas profesiones. Es posible que el trabajo sea muy diferente.
b1-31-02.english: There will probably be new professions. It is possible that work will be very different.
b1-31-02.canDo: I can express predictions with different levels of certainty.

b1-31-03.title: Communicative Challenge: What If?
b1-31-03.scenario: You are Meg. Your sister Kaylee asks what you and Carlos would do if he had no job at his office in Budapest. You say that you would have to adapt.
b1-31-03.prompt: Tell Kaylee what would happen and what you would do.
cues: Say what would change
Say what you would have to do
b1-31-03.target: Si Carlos no tuviera trabajo, tendríamos que adaptarnos.
b1-31-03.english: If Carlos had no job, we would have to adapt.
b1-31-03.canDo: I can discuss hypothetical changes and consequences.

b1-31-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Getting Ready
b1-31-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what the two of you should do to prepare for the coming years in Budapest. You say it is important to learn new skills and necessary to prepare.
b1-31-04.prompt: Tell Meg what is important and what is necessary.
cues: Say what is important to learn
Say what is necessary to do
b1-31-04.target: Es importante que aprendamos nuevas habilidades y es necesario que nos preparemos.
b1-31-04.english: It is important that we learn new skills and it is necessary that we prepare.
b1-31-04.canDo: I can discuss how society should prepare for change.

b1-31-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Calibán and Ariel
b1-31-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the text about Rubén Darío says. In 1898 Darío called the United States Calibán, a country of force, money and machines, and put Ariel, art and ideals, with the Latin peoples. He asked the Latin nations to unite.
b1-31-05.prompt: Tell Carlos who Calibán is for Darío and what Darío asks of the Latin nations.
cues: Say who Darío calls Calibán
Say what Ariel is for Darío
Say what Darío asks of the nations
b1-31-05.target: Darío llama Calibán a Estados Unidos, un país de dinero y máquinas. Ariel es el arte y las ideas, y Darío pide a los países de América que estén unidos.
b1-31-05.english: Darío calls the United States Calibán, a country of money and machines. Ariel is art and ideas, and Darío asks the countries of America to be united.
b1-31-05.canDo: I can discuss the future of society in a sustained way.

b1-31-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: An Uncertain Future
b1-31-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think about the next ten years. You say that there will probably be many changes, that you would have to adapt if they were fast, and that it is important to prepare.
b1-31-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what will probably happen and how to prepare.
cues: Say what will probably happen
Say what you would do if it were fast
Say what is important
b1-31-consolidation.target: Probablemente habrá muchos cambios. Si fueran rápidos, tendríamos que adaptarnos, así que es importante que nos preparemos.
b1-31-consolidation.english: There will probably be many changes. If they were fast, we would have to adapt, so it is important that we prepare.
b1-31-consolidation.canDo: I can use the vocabulary of the future and probability.

b1-32-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Were You Late?
b1-32-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you arrived late to dinner in Budapest. There was a lot of snow and the trams were slow.
b1-32-01.prompt: Tell Meg why you were late.
cues: Say that you were late
Give the cause using a connector
b1-32-01.target: Llegué tarde a la cena debido a la nieve.
b1-32-01.english: I arrived late to dinner because of the snow.
b1-32-01.canDo: I can explain causes and reasons clearly.

b1-32-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Cancelled Dinner
b1-32-02.scenario: You are Meg. Your sister Kaylee asks on a call why you and Carlos cancelled dinner with friends. The train was late and you had little time.
b1-32-02.prompt: Tell Kaylee what happened and what the result was.
cues: Say what happened
Say what you did as a result
b1-32-02.target: El tren llegó tarde, por eso cancelamos la cena.
b1-32-02.english: The train was late, so we cancelled dinner.
b1-32-02.canDo: I can explain consequences and results.

b1-32-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Studying Despite Work
b1-32-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how you find time for Spanish with your job at the office in Budapest. You work a lot, but you study every day.
b1-32-03.prompt: Tell Meg that you study Spanish although you work a lot.
cues: Say that you work a lot
Say that you study anyway
b1-32-03.target: A pesar de que trabajo mucho en la oficina, estudio español todos los días.
b1-32-03.english: Although I work a lot at the office, I study Spanish every day.
b1-32-03.canDo: I can contrast ideas and concede a point.

b1-32-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Spanish?
b1-32-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you practise Spanish every day. You want to talk with his grandmother in Madrid, and you want her to understand you.
b1-32-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what you study for and why.
cues: Say what you study
Say your purpose
Say whom you want to talk to
b1-32-04.target: Estudio español para hablar con tu abuela de Madrid y para que ella me entienda.
b1-32-04.english: I study Spanish to talk with your grandmother in Madrid and so that she understands me.
b1-32-04.canDo: I can explain purposes and objectives.

b1-32-05.title: Communicative Challenge: An Article About Habits
b1-32-05.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what the article you read says. The writer asks why people in his city stroll in the evening and not in the morning: in the morning almost everyone works, and at midday it is hot.
b1-32-05.prompt: Tell Meg what the writer asks and what reasons he gives.
cues: Say what the writer asks
Give the reason for the morning
Give the reason for the midday
b1-32-05.target: El autor se pregunta por qué la gente pasea por la tarde. Por la mañana casi todos trabajan y a mediodía hace calor, así que esperan hasta la tarde.
b1-32-05.english: The writer asks why people stroll in the evening. In the morning almost everyone works and at midday it is hot, so they wait until the evening.
b1-32-05.canDo: I can build a connected argument.

b1-32-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Moving Flats
b1-32-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what you think about moving to a flat in the centre of Budapest. It is expensive, but it is close to his office and to your university.
b1-32-consolidation.prompt: Give Carlos your argument for and against the flat.
cues: Say the cost
Contrast it with a good point
Say what you conclude
b1-32-consolidation.target: El piso del centro es caro; sin embargo, está cerca de tu oficina y de mis clases. Por eso creo que es una buena idea.
b1-32-consolidation.english: The flat in the centre is expensive; however, it is close to your office and my university. So I think it is a good idea.
b1-32-consolidation.canDo: I can use the main connectors of the unit.

b1-33-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Did Ana Say?
b1-33-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what your sister Ana said when she called from Budapest this morning. Ana said: “I am tired and I cannot come.”
b1-33-01.prompt: Tell Meg what Ana said, without repeating her exact words.
cues: Say who spoke
Say how she felt
Say what she could not do
b1-33-01.target: Ana dijo que estaba cansada y que no podía venir.
b1-33-01.english: Ana said that she was tired and that she could not come.
b1-33-01.canDo: I can distinguish direct and indirect speech.

b1-33-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Lauren Has No Time
b1-33-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what your sister Lauren told you in her message. She wrote that she had no time to call this week.
b1-33-02.prompt: Tell Carlos what Lauren told you.
cues: Say who wrote to you
Say what she told you about time
b1-33-02.target: Lauren me dijo que no tenía tiempo para llamar esta semana.
b1-33-02.english: Lauren told me that she did not have time to call this week.

b1-33-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Grandmother's Questions
b1-33-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what your grandmother in Madrid wanted to know when she called you. She asked: “Do you have time?” and “Where do you work now?”
b1-33-03.prompt: Tell Meg what your grandmother asked you.
cues: Say who asked you
Report her yes/no question
Report her question about work
b1-33-03.target: Mi abuela me preguntó si tenía tiempo y dónde trabajaba ahora.
b1-33-03.english: My grandmother asked me if I had time and where I worked now.
b1-33-03.canDo: I can report yes/no and information questions.

b1-33-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Kaylee's Call
b1-33-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what Kaylee said when she called you from her flat in South Africa. She said: “I live here with a friend, and tomorrow I am going to Lauren's.”
b1-33-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what Kaylee said, from your point of view.
cues: Say where and with whom she lived
Say what she was doing the next day
b1-33-04.target: Kaylee dijo que vivía allí con una amiga y que al día siguiente iba a casa de Lauren.
b1-33-04.english: Kaylee said that she lived there with a friend and that the next day she was going to Lauren's house.
b1-33-04.canDo: I can reconstruct a conversation from another perspective.

b1-33-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rumour in Lima
b1-33-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a story about a rumour in colonial Lima for a class in Budapest, and Carlos asks what it is about. Doña Mariquita told a neighbour that she had seen the sacristan leave the cathedral with a heavy bag; later the sacristan told the viceroy that it held only old candles.
b1-33-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what doña Mariquita told her neighbour and what the sacristan answered the viceroy.
cues: Say what doña Mariquita told her neighbour
Say what the sacristan answered
b1-33-05.target: Doña Mariquita contó a una vecina que había visto al sacristán con una bolsa muy pesada. El sacristán respondió al virrey que en la bolsa solo había velas viejas.
b1-33-05.english: Doña Mariquita told a neighbour that she had seen the sacristan with a very heavy bag. The sacristan answered the viceroy that there were only old candles in the bag.
b1-33-05.canDo: I can reconstruct what happened using reported speech.

b1-33-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Andreas Called
b1-33-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what your brother Andreas said when he called yesterday evening. He said he was tired, and he asked: “Do you have time this weekend?”
b1-33-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what Andreas said and what he asked you.
cues: Say how he felt
Report his question about the weekend
b1-33-consolidation.target: Andreas dijo que estaba cansado y me preguntó si tenía tiempo el fin de semana.
b1-33-consolidation.english: Andreas said that he was tired and asked me if I had time at the weekend.
b1-33-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate direct and indirect speech.

b1-34-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Changing the Class Day
b1-34-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos suggests moving your Spanish class in Budapest to Saturday. You do not think a change is necessary because the day you have now works well.
b1-34-01.prompt: Tell Carlos politely that you do not think a change is necessary.
cues: Say you do not think a change is necessary
Say what is good about the day you have now
b1-34-01.target: No creo que sea necesario cambiar el día de la clase. Creo que el día de ahora es bueno.
b1-34-01.english: I don't think it is necessary to change the day of the class. I think the current day is good.
b1-34-01.canDo: I can express opinions with negation and doubt.

b1-34-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Will Ana Visit?
b1-34-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if your sister Ana will visit you in Budapest. You do not know yet, but she may come this month.
b1-34-02.prompt: Tell Meg that Ana may come, but it is not certain.
cues: Say it is possible that Ana comes
Say on which day she might arrive
b1-34-02.target: Es posible que Ana venga a Budapest este mes. Quizá llegue el sábado.
b1-34-02.english: It is possible that Ana will come to Budapest this month. Perhaps she will arrive on Saturday.
b1-34-02.canDo: I can express possibility and uncertainty.

b1-34-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Spanish Exam
b1-34-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks how you feel about your Spanish exam in Budapest. You are sure you understand the grammar, but you are not sure you speak well.
b1-34-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you are sure about and what you are not sure about.
cues: Say what you are sure about
Say what you are not sure about
b1-34-03.target: Estoy segura de que entiendo la gramática, pero no estoy segura de que hable bien en el examen.
b1-34-03.english: I am sure that I understand the grammar, but I am not sure that I speak well in the exam.
b1-34-03.canDo: I can contrast certainty and doubt.

b1-34-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Flat
b1-34-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what matters to you in the flat you want to rent in Budapest. It is important to you that it is near the metro, and it worries you that it may be too expensive.
b1-34-04.prompt: Tell Meg what is important to you and what worries you.
cues: Say what is important about the location
Say what worries you
b1-34-04.target: Es importante que el piso esté cerca del metro, pero me preocupa que sea muy caro.
b1-34-04.english: It is important that the flat is near the metro, but it worries me that it may be very expensive.
b1-34-04.canDo: I can express evaluations about actions and situations.

b1-34-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Debate in the Cafés
b1-34-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read an article for your class in Budapest about a debate in the cafés of Madrid: is the new theatre better than the old? Carlos asks what the writer thinks. The writer does not believe it is a simple question, doubts that the new theatre is better in everything, and finds it important that every opinion rests on reasons.
b1-34-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the writer thinks.
cues: Say what the writer does not believe
Say what he doubts
Say what he finds important
b1-34-05.target: El autor no cree que el tema sea sencillo. Duda que el teatro nuevo sea mejor en todo y piensa que es importante que cada opinión tenga razones.
b1-34-05.english: The writer does not believe the topic is simple. He doubts that the new theatre is better in everything and thinks it is important that every opinion has reasons.
b1-34-05.canDo: I can give a nuanced opinion rather than a simple yes-or-no judgement.

b1-34-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Trip in Summer
b1-34-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you want to travel to Valencia together in the summer. You are sure it would be a nice trip, but you do not think you have enough time. Perhaps August is possible.
b1-34-consolidation.prompt: Give Meg your balanced answer about the trip.
cues: Say what you are sure about
Say what you do not believe
Say what is possible
b1-34-consolidation.target: Estoy seguro de que sería un viaje bonito, pero no creo que tengamos tiempo. Es posible que podamos ir en agosto.
b1-34-consolidation.english: I am sure it would be a nice trip, but I don't think we have time. It is possible that we can go in August.
b1-34-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate the main opinion structures.

b1-35-01.title: Communicative Challenge: If I Could Choose
b1-35-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks where you would study if you could choose any place. You would choose to spend a year in Madrid, where his grandmother lives.
b1-35-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what you would choose if you had the option.
cues: Say that you imagine having the option
Say what you would choose
b1-35-01.target: Si tuviera la opción, estudiaría un año en Madrid.
b1-35-01.english: If I had the option, I would study for a year in Madrid.
b1-35-01.canDo: I can express hypothetical choices and preferences.

b1-35-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Week of Rain
b1-35-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what would happen if it rained all week in Budapest. You would not go out, and you would work at home.
b1-35-02.prompt: Tell Meg what would happen if it rained all week.
cues: Say the imagined condition
Say what you would not do
Say what you would do instead
b1-35-02.target: Si lloviera toda la semana, no saldríamos y yo trabajaría en casa.
b1-35-02.english: If it rained all week, we would not go out and I would work at home.

b1-35-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Missed Concert
b1-35-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks why you did not go to the concert last Friday. You had an exam the next morning. Without the exam, you would have gone.
b1-35-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what would have happened without the exam.
cues: Say what you had
Say what you would have done
b1-35-03.target: Si no hubiera tenido un examen, habría ido al concierto.
b1-35-03.english: If I had not had an exam, I would have gone to the concert.
b1-35-03.canDo: I can refer to unreal past situations.

b1-35-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Summer Plans
b1-35-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you would do with two free weeks in the summer. You could visit your grandmother in Madrid. If that were not possible, you would stay in Budapest.
cues: Say what you could do with two weeks
Say what you would do if that were not possible
b1-35-04.target: Si tuviera dos semanas libres, podría visitar a mi abuela en Madrid. Si no fuera posible, me quedaría en Budapest.
b1-35-04.english: If I had two free weeks, I could visit my grandmother in Madrid. If it were not possible, I would stay in Budapest.

b1-35-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Green Eyes
b1-35-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read the legend of the green eyes for your class in Budapest, and Carlos asks what happens. Íñigo warned Fernando that an evil spirit lived in the spring of Los Álamos, but Fernando kept going back there.
b1-35-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Íñigo said and what would have happened if Fernando had listened.
cues: Say what Íñigo said about the spring
Say what Fernando would not have done if he had listened
b1-35-05.target: Íñigo le dijo a Fernando que en la fuente vivía un espíritu del mal. Si Fernando hubiera hecho caso, no habría vuelto a la fuente.
b1-35-05.english: Íñigo told Fernando that an evil spirit lived in the spring. If Fernando had listened, he would not have gone back to the spring.
b1-35-05.canDo: I can reflect on choices and alternatives.

b1-35-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: More Time for Spanish
b1-35-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you wish you had studied more Spanish before moving to Budapest. You did not have much time then, and you still do not have much time now.
b1-35-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what you would have done and what you would do with more time.
cues: Say what you would have done with more time before
Say what you would do now with more time
b1-35-consolidation.target: Si hubiera tenido más tiempo, habría estudiado español antes. Si tuviera más tiempo ahora, estudiaría todos los días.
b1-35-consolidation.english: If I had had more time, I would have studied Spanish earlier. If I had more time now, I would study every day.
b1-35-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate present/future hypothetical structures.

b1-36-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Meeting
b1-36-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks how the meeting at your office in Budapest went this morning. You arrived late: the meeting had already started. Afterwards you talked with your colleagues and understood the plan.
b1-36-01.prompt: Tell Meg what happened, in order.
cues: Say what had already happened when you arrived
Say what you did afterwards
b1-36-01.target: Cuando llegué, ya había empezado la reunión. Después de hablar con mis compañeros, entendí el plan.
b1-36-01.english: When I arrived, the meeting had already started. After talking with my colleagues, I understood the plan.
b1-36-01.canDo: I can tell a connected story using familiar B1 narrative structures.

b1-36-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Online Lessons
b1-36-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos suggests taking your Spanish lessons online because it is cheaper. You understand the argument, but you do not think it is the best option, and you are convinced that you need to speak with people.
b1-36-02.prompt: Tell Carlos your position and why.
cues: Say what you do not think
Acknowledge his argument
Say what you are convinced of
b1-36-02.target: No creo que sea la mejor opción, aunque entiendo el argumento. Estoy convencida de que necesito hablar con personas.
b1-36-02.english: I don't think it is the best option, although I understand the argument. I am convinced that I need to talk with people.
b1-36-02.canDo: I can explain and defend a position.

b1-36-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Problem at the Office
b1-36-03.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about a problem at your office in Budapest: some colleagues arrive at the wrong time because nobody tells them the new schedule.
b1-36-03.prompt: Tell Meg the problem, its cause and what is necessary.
cues: Say the cause of the problem
Say what is necessary
b1-36-03.target: El problema existe porque falta información sobre el horario. Por eso, es necesario que busquemos una solución.
b1-36-03.english: The problem exists because information about the schedule is missing. Therefore, it is necessary that we look for a solution.
b1-36-03.canDo: I can explain a problem and its causes.

b1-36-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Next Year
b1-36-04.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks about your plans for next year. It is possible that you will travel to Madrid. If you had more money, you would also travel to Chile to see Daniela.
b1-36-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what is possible and what you would do with more money.
cues: Say what is possible
Say what you would do with more money
b1-36-04.target: Es posible que viaje a Madrid. Si tuviera más dinero, viajaría también a Chile para ver a Daniela.
b1-36-04.english: It is possible that I will travel to Madrid. If I had more money, I would also travel to Chile to see Daniela.
b1-36-04.canDo: I can discuss future possibilities and alternatives.

b1-36-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Marta's Story
b1-36-05.scenario: You are Meg. You read a story about a woman called Marta for your class in Budapest, and Carlos asks what it says. Marta does not think a perfect solution exists, but she thinks it is important to listen to different opinions. In her community, some people arrive late because the transport does not work well.
b1-36-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what Marta thinks and what the problem is.
cues: Say what Marta does not believe
Say what she finds important
Say the problem in her community
b1-36-05.target: Marta no cree que exista una solución perfecta, pero cree que es importante escuchar diferentes opiniones. En su comunidad, algunas personas llegan tarde porque el transporte no funciona bien.
b1-36-05.english: Marta does not believe that a perfect solution exists, but she believes it is important to listen to different opinions. In her community, some people arrive late because the transport does not work well.
b1-36-05.canDo: I can communicate independently across familiar B1 situations.

b1-36-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Working from Home
b1-36-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think about working from home two days a week at your office in Budapest. You are not sure it is a perfect solution, but you are convinced it can help, and you think you must talk with your boss.
b1-36-consolidation.prompt: Give Meg your opinion and say what is necessary.
cues: Say what you do not believe
Say what you are convinced of
Say what is necessary
b1-36-consolidation.target: No creo que sea una solución perfecta, pero estoy convencido de que puede ayudar. Es necesario que hablemos con el jefe.
b1-36-consolidation.english: I don't think it is a perfect solution, but I am convinced that it can help. It is necessary that we talk with the boss.
b1-36-consolidation.canDo: I can retrieve the main B1 structures in connected communication.
